Section 3.02(b) states that every person who is not a Member and who the Vice President determines to be an Eligible Employee shall be admitted to Membership following approval by the Vice President, effective as of the Entry Date coinciding with or immediately following the date their Service commences or they become an Eligible Employee (whichever is later), and no Eligible Employee or other person shall be admitted to or continue in Membership without Vice President approval. Article IV – Requirements for Benefits states that a Member is entitled to a Normal Retirement Pension if employment with both their Employer and the PepsiCo Organization terminates on their Normal Retirement Age; the Member’s Annuity Starting Date is the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following termination of employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization; the Pension is paid in the normal form under Section 5.02 unless the Member elects an optional form under Section 5.03; the Pension is calculated according to Table A. A Member is entitled to an Early Retirement Pension if employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization terminates on or after age 55 but before Normal Retirement Age and after completing 10 or more years of Service; the Annuity Starting Date is ordinarily the Normal Retirement Date, but the Member may file a written election with the Vice President to set it as the first day of any month after termination but before Normal Retirement Date; the Pension amount is computed as if retiring at Normal Retirement Age using the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary (as defined in Table A) and Pensionable Service as of termination date, but if the Pension is received before age 62, it is reduced by 4/12 of 1 percent for each month before the Member would have reached age 62. A Member may be entitled to a Special Early Retirement Pension if employment terminates on or after age 50 but before age 55, after completing at least 10 years of Service, and only if authorized by the Vice President; the Annuity Starting Date is the first day of the month after the Vice President authorizes the Special Early Retirement Pension; the Pension amount is computed as if retiring at Normal Retirement Age using the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination date, but is reduced by 4/12 of 1 percent for each month before the Member would have reached age 62. Section 4.04 Deferred Vested Pension begins with (a).

A Member may be entitled to a Special Early Retirement Pension if their employment with both their Employer and the PepsiCo Organization ends on or after age 50 but before age 55 and after completing at least 10 years of Service, provided such pension is authorized by the Vice President. The Annuity Starting Date for this pension is the first day of the month following the Vice President’s authorization. The pension amount is calculated using Table A as if the Member retired at their Normal Retirement Date, based on their Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of their employment termination date, but is reduced by 4/12 of 1 percent for each month the pension commences before the Member would have reached age 62. A Member who terminates employment with both their Employer and the PepsiCo Organization before becoming eligible for a Normal Retirement Pension, Early Retirement Pension, or Special Early Retirement Pension may be entitled to a Deferred Vested Pension if they meet the vesting requirements in Sections 4.06 or 4.07. The amount of the Deferred Vested Pension is determined in accordance with Table A using the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary at termination (subject to Sections 9.13 and 9.14) and their Pensionable Service as of termination. The pension commences on the later of (i) the termination of employment or (ii) the Member’s Normal Retirement Date, though the Member may elect, by filing a written election with the Vice President, to have it commence on the first day of any month after the Member attains age 55 (or after termination, if later). If the Member receives the pension before their Normal Retirement Date, the amount is reduced according to the reduction factors for early commencement of a “Vested Pension” under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan, not those for Early or Special Early Retirement Pensions. If the Member becomes entitled to a Deferred Vested Pension and later becomes an Eligible Employee again, they are re-admitted to Active Membership under Article III, and their prior Service and Pensionable Service are aggregated with subsequent Service and Pensionable Service for pension calculations upon later retirement, provided the prior pension was not previously cashed out under Section 5.05. A Member who continues employment with the PepsiCo Organization or any Employer after reaching their Normal Retirement Age is entitled to a Late Retirement Pension, with the Annuity Starting Date being the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following termination of employment with both the Employer and PepsiCo Organization. The Member is credited with Salary and Pensionable Service after their Normal Retirement Date unless otherwise prospectively determined by the Vice President. A Member is fully vested in their Pension upon completing 5 years of Service or, if earlier, upon death or disability while employed, with disability determined by the Vice President using standards deemed appropriate at the time. An Active Member who will have an Approved Transfer during a Plan Year automatically achieves special vesting as of the last business day before the earlier of (a) the Approved Transfer or (b) the day they would become a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer. Similarly, an Active Member may request special vesting as of the last business day before a Status Change, with both the request and Vice President’s approval required to be final and in place prior to the date of application. The effect of special vesting under either (a) or (b) is that the Member becomes vested to the same extent as under Section 4.06, subject to the requirement that benefits remain exempt from Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code and that this Section 4.07 does not apply to the extent inconsistent with that requirement. A Member who earns Service and Pensionable Service after their Annuity Starting Date under prior Sections of Article IV (excluding a cashout under Section 5.05) will have any prior suspended benefits and additional accrued benefits paid at their subsequent Annuity Starting Date. The suspension or continuation of prior benefits, adjustments to benefits at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date, and elections of payment time and form are subject to rules established by the Vice President, based on the PepsiCo Salaried Plan’s rules for benefits accrued after benefit commencement, unless the Vice President determines a modification is appropriate. Under Article V, distribution options include normal forms of payment: unmarried Members receive a Single Life Annuity unless they elect otherwise; married Members receive a 50 Percent Survivor Annuity unless they elect otherwise, with the pension amount reduced by 10 percent for Annuity Starting Dates before January 1, 2019, except for members entitled to a pension under the Plan prior to January 1, 1990, whose pension is not subject to this reduction. For Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019, the pension amount is reduced to its Actuarial Equivalent to reflect the survivor benefit. Married Members may also elect optional forms of payment, including a Single Life Annuity or a 75 Percent Survivor Annuity, regardless of eligibility for other options. Survivor options include a 100 Percent Survivor Option (with a 20 percent reduction for pre-January 1, 2019, starting dates, subject to subsection (f)), a 75 Percent Survivor Option (with a 15 percent reduction for pre-January 1, 2019, starting dates), and a 50 Percent Survivor Option (with a 10 percent reduction for pre-January 1, 2019, starting dates, not applicable to members entitled to a pension prior to January 1, 1990). A Ten-Year Certain and Life Option allows monthly payments for at least 120 months, with post-death payments to a primary or contingent Dependant or estate, and effective January 1, 2010, the Dependant or estate may elect a lump sum equal to the actuarial equivalent of remaining payments (without mortality reduction). A Lump Sum Payment option allows a single lump sum equal to the actuarial equivalent of the Single Life Annuity, calculated using lump sum equivalent factors from the PepsiCo Salaried Plan (excluding transition factors), paid within one taxable year and as soon as practicable after the Member’s specified date, with interest added to late payments after January 1, 2010, but no interest during any deferred period. A Combination Lump Sum/Monthly Benefit allows a portion in lump sum and the remainder in monthly payments, with the percentages adding to 100 percent. The lump sum amount is calculated by multiplying the amount under Section 5.03(c) by the designated lump sum percentage, and the monthly amount by the designated monthly percentage. If a Member entitled to an immediate pension under Article IV elects an optional form of payment and dies after leaving employment but before the pension becomes payable, the optional form of payment begins on the first day of the month following death.

The amount of a lump sum benefit is determined by multiplying the amount established under Section 5.03(c) by the percentage the Member has designated for receipt as a lump sum. The amount of a monthly benefit is calculated by multiplying the monthly benefit elected by the Member, as determined under Sections 5.03(a) or (b), by the percentage designated for monthly payments. If a Member entitled to an immediate Pension under Article IV elects an optional form of payment under Section 5.03 and meets all requirements (excluding survival, but including timely election and any required consent from an Eligible Spouse), and dies after leaving employment but before the Pension becomes payable, the optional form of payment is deemed effective on the first day of the month following death. This deemed effectiveness applies only once and only to the initial election, except as permitted by a prior decision of the Vice President regarding a subsequent purported election. However, for the option under Section 5.03(b), if the specified Dependant dies or shall die before the first installment of the Pension is prospectively payable under the elected form, the election is not effective. For annuities starting before January 1, 2019, if a Dependant is more than 10 years younger than the Member, the Pension is reduced: if the Dependant is more than 10 but not more than 20 years younger, the reduction percentage is increased by 5 percentage points; if the Dependant is more than 20 years younger, the 5 percentage point increase is further increased by an additional 0.2 percent for each full year over 20. Section 5.04 restricts certain distribution options: the form in Section 5.03(d) is not available unless the Member’s Annuity Starting Date is after 1989; Deferred Vested Pensions under Section 4.04 are eligible only for the Single Life Annuity, the 50 Percent Survivor Option, or the 75 Percent Survivor Option, except that effective January 1, 2015, they may also be eligible for the Lump Sum Payment option, but only if available on an ongoing basis under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan, and participants in the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan are not excluded from this option. For Members who became entitled to a Pension before January 1, 1990, actuarial equivalencies are adjusted by the Vice President to reflect the value of any subsidized survivor benefit under Section 5.02(b). Under Section 5.05, if the total Pension payable is deemed relatively trivial by the Vice President, the entire Pension may be commuted to a lump sum payable after the Member’s termination of employment from both employer and PepsiCo Organization, or after a transfer within PepsiCo that ends accrual of DB benefits, on a date set by the Vice President without Member consent. Effective January 1, 2019, the Vice President may make a lump-sum payment to any Member whose benefit has commenced (not in lump sum form) if the present value of the remaining payments is less than or equal to $75,000 on the payment date; the lump sum amount equals the actuarial equivalent of the remaining payments, calculated using the lump sum equivalent factors in Section 5.03(c) as of a date set by the Vice President. A Member who elects a payment form with a survivor option must designate a Dependant entitled to benefits upon death; the designation may be changed or revoked at any time before the election’s effective date. If the Member is married at the time of designation, naming a Dependant other than the Eligible Spouse requires the Eligible Spouse’s written consent; revocation of a Dependant does not require consent. All designations, changes, revocations, and consents must be in writing on forms provided by the Vice President and filed with the Vice President to be effective. For the survivor option in Section 5.03(b)(4), the Member may name both a primary and a contingent Dependant; if no Dependant is properly designated, the election is not effective. Under Article VI, a surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner is entitled to survivor benefits if the requirements are met, with the benefit amount determined according to Section II of Table A. For an Active Member, a Member in Service after Normal Retirement Date with at least 5 years of Service, or a Member entitled to an Early Retirement Pension or Special Early Retirement Pension who is survived by an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner and not entitled to protection under Section 5.03(e), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable, calculated under Section II of Table A. For a vested Member not covered in Section 6.01, who has not yet commenced or received a Pension, and who is survived by an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner and not entitled to protection under Section 5.03(e), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable, calculated based on the Member’s Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of death or termination of employment, as if the Member had lived until the earliest date their vested benefit could have started with a 50 Percent Survivor Annuity and died that day. This benefit is paid by reducing the monthly benefit otherwise payable to the Member, using the same methodology and factors as in the PepsiCo Salaried Plan, and the Member may only waive this coverage with Vice President approval. Any Pension payable under Article VI is payable for the surviving Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner’s life only, except that if the Member was eligible for a Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement Pension at death, the surviving spouse or partner may elect a single lump sum payment instead of an annuity. The benefit commences on the first day of the month coinciding with or next following the Member’s death, or if later, the date the Member would have reached age 55; if the benefit commences before the Member would have reached Normal Retirement Age, it is reduced as set forth in Sections 4.02, 4.03, or 4.04, as applicable. Any benefit subject to disposition under Article VI is held by the Vice President, who has the power to pay or apply it to or for the benefit of one or more of the Member’s dependants as they see fit, and may direct the benefit to commence or be paid as a lump sum as soon as practicable after the Member’s death. The Plan is administered by the Vice President, who has the authority to interpret the Plan and issue regulations, and all actions and interpretations are final and binding. The Vice President may delegate responsibilities to others, and any reference to the Vice President may refer to a delegate or designated person. If a person entitled to a benefit is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the person’s benefit, and such payment constitutes a complete discharge of liability. The Vice President has exclusive discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and all decisions are final and conclusive. This discretion is absolute and will be reviewed under the arbitrary and capricious standard by a court, arbitrator, or tribunal. If a claim for benefits is denied, the Vice President or a designated party must provide a written notice within 90 days that includes the specific reasons for denial, references to relevant Plan provisions, a description of any additional material needed to perfect the claim, and a description of the claim review procedure, including time limits. If special circumstances require an extension, the period may be extended from 90 to 180 days, with notice given before the end of the initial 90-day period. Upon review, the Vice President must provide a full and fair review, including the opportunity to submit comments, documents, and records, and the review must consider such submissions regardless of whether they were considered initially. The decision on review is made within 60 days after receipt of the request, unless extended by up to an additional 60 days with prior notice. The final decision must be in writing, understandable to the claimant, include specific reasons and references to Plan provisions, and provide that the claimant is entitled, upon request and free of charge, to copies of all relevant documents, records, and information. Any claim reviewed by a court, arbitrator, or tribunal is reviewed solely on the record before the Vice President’s initial determination and only after the claimant has fully exhausted all rights under this section and Section 7.07. Any claim filed under Article VII or any action in court or tribunal by a former or current Employee, Member, Dependant, or other individual must be brought within two years of when the cause of action first accrues, which is deemed to be not later than the earlier of (i) when the claimant receives the benefit calculation, (ii) the date identified by the Vice President for payment commencement, or (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts underlying the claim. Failure to file within this two-year period precludes the claim or action.

Any claim for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits by a former or current Employee, Member, Dependant, or any other individual, person, or entity (a “Petitioner”) must be filed within two years of the date the Petitioner’s cause of action first accrues. For this purpose, a cause of action accrues not later than the earlier of (i) when the Petitioner receives the calculation of the benefits at issue, (ii) the date identified by the Vice President on which payments are to commence, or (iii) when the Petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts supporting the claim. Failure to file within this two-year period will preclude the Petitioner or any representative from bringing the claim. Communications following the mandatory appeals process described in Section 7.03 do not extend or affect this two-year limitation. Any claim or action related to the Plan must be brought only in the state or federal courts of New York, specifically the one nearest the Corporation’s headquarters. Specific references in the Plan to the Vice President’s discretion do not imply that such discretion is less broad in any other context. Before filing any claim, suit, or action in court or another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all rights under the claims procedure in Section 7.03. This exhaustion requirement applies regardless of whether other Disputes are more significant, to any rights the Vice President may provide, whether actual or potential, and even if no specific procedures exist for the claim—where no procedures exist, the Vice President must either promptly establish them or apply the procedures in Section 7.03. The Vice President may make special arrangements to consider claims on a class basis or address unusual conflicts, but such arrangements must ensure exhaustion is required to the maximum extent. A “Dispute” includes any claim, issue, assertion, or matter, and a “Claim” is any Dispute that involves (A) the interpretation of the Plan, (B) any term or condition of the Plan, (C) the interpretation of the Plan in light of applicable law, (D) whether the Plan has been validly adopted, (E) the administration of the Plan, (F) whether the Plan has violated applicable law or regulation, (G) a request for or attempt to recover Plan benefits, (H) an assertion of a legal duty, or (I) any claim deemed similar by the Vice President or relating to the Plan. A “Claimant” includes any actual or putative Eligible Employee, former Employee, Member, former Member, Dependant, spouse, former spouse, estate, heir, or representative thereof, or any other individual, person, or entity with a relationship to such individuals or the Plan, or a group of such individuals. The Vice President intends to interpret and operate the Plan in good faith and in compliance with applicable law, and the requirement to exhaust claims is contractual and intended to ensure efficient, uniform resolution and to prevent substantial litigation costs. While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely, it makes no contractual commitment to do so and reserves the right to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time, provided that no such action adversely affects the benefit amount of a Member or Dependant on the date of amendment or termination, unless the Member becomes entitled to an equivalent benefit under another Corporation plan or practice. Specific forms of payment are not protected. Amendments may be made by the Corporation in its sole discretion, with or without retroactive effect, and no Employer other than the Corporation may amend the Plan. If the Plan is terminated with respect to fewer than all Employers, it continues for the benefit of employees of the remaining Employers. The Employers’ obligations under the Plan are unfunded and constitute liabilities payable from their general funds, and rights to benefits are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors. All costs, charges, and expenses of Plan administration are borne by the Employers and allocated based on the proportion of Members employed by each Employer. If a Member is absent from duty for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation), they are deemed to have terminated employment 12 months after the absence begins, unless the Vice President determines otherwise. If the absence is due to full-time service in the armed forces or national service, the Member is not deemed terminated so long as the Employer considers them in employment or until they resign permanently, whichever occurs first. If the Vice President determines that a benefit is subject to a tax or assessment, the Plan may withhold up to the amount of such tax or duty from the benefit and apply it to satisfy the obligation. Nothing in the Plan constitutes a contract of employment, a right to continue employment, or a limitation on an Employer’s right to discharge employees. No person has a claim, right, or interest under the Plan except as provided in the Plan, and termination of employment is not grounds for damages. All benefits are subject to deductions for losses caused by a Member’s misdemeanor, with proof required by the Member to the satisfaction of the Vice President. Any overpayment, premature payment, or misdirected payment (an “Excess Payment”) must be restored promptly to the Plan. In exchange for receiving an Excess Payment, the recipient grants the Plan a constructive trust and first priority equitable lien on the Excess Payment or its proceeds, increased by appropriate interest, and the right to offset future payments from the Plan, at the Vice President’s discretion. The recipient also waives any rights to jurisdiction based on residence and submits to any court of competent jurisdiction for enforcement. The recipient must take all actions requested by the Vice President to recover the Excess Payment. This subsection maximizes the Plan’s rights to recover improper payments and does not restrict those rights. A Member forfeits their Pension if the Vice President determines they were terminated for cause or engaged in Prohibited Misconduct prior to the second anniversary of employment termination, and any previously paid Pension must be recovered. Prohibited Misconduct includes (1) accepting employment or ownership in a business that markets, sells, distributes, or produces “Covered Products” (such as beverages, juices, dairy, snacks, cereals, and value-added products) unless the business makes retail sales or consumes such products without competing with PepsiCo, (2) soliciting a PepsiCo employee to leave or join another entity, (3) using or disclosing confidential information (including customer, supplier, financial, operational, or strategic data) not necessary for their role, (4) engaging in acts contrary to PepsiCo’s best interests, including violating the Code of Conduct, unlawful trading based on insider information, or gross misconduct, and (5) engaging in fraud. Notwithstanding these provisions, Members may communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations without notice, participate in investigations, or receive awards for such disclosures, and the Corporation retains attorney-client privilege. Under the Defend Trade Secrets Act, individuals are not liable for disclosing trade secrets to government officials or attorneys for reporting suspected violations, or in sealed complaints, and may use such information in court proceedings if filed under seal and not disclosed except by court order. “Participation” includes serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor, providing input, advice, guidance, or recommendations, or giving a testimonial on behalf of a business entity. “Covered Products” include any product in categories such as beverages, juices, dairy, snacks, cereals, and value-added food products, wherever PepsiCo produces, markets, sells, or licenses them.

The trade secret is kept under seal and is not disclosed except pursuant to a court order. For the purposes of this subsection, “Participation” is broadly defined to include serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor with respect to a business entity; providing input, advice, guidance, or suggestions to such a business entity; or providing a recommendation or testimonial on behalf of such a business entity or one or more products it produces. “Covered Products” refers to any product that falls into one or more of the following categories—beverages (including carbonated soft drinks, tea, water, juice drinks, sports drinks, coffee drinks, energy drinks, and value-added dairy drinks), juices and juice products, dairy products, snacks (including salty snacks, sweet snacks, meat snacks, granola and cereal bars, and cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes, value-added rice products, pancake syrups, value-added pasta products, ready-to-eat cereals, dry pasta products, or any product or service that the Member had reason to know was under development by the PepsiCo Organization during their employment with PepsiCo. Any notice required under the Plan to be given to or served upon the Plan is deemed sufficient if it is in writing and delivered to the Vice President. If notice is required to be given to Members, it is sufficient if delivered to the Member’s last known address on file or via any other method (e.g., electronically) that the Vice President determines is reasonably available to the Member. Every Member is entitled on demand to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program. Benefits under the Plan are paid in United States dollars or other “eligible currency” as approved by the Vice President, with amounts otherwise payable in U.S. dollars converted to the selected currency using an exchange rate based on a methodology approved by the Vice President from time to time. The Plan is governed by and interpreted according to the laws of the State of New York. The Plan is intended to be exempt from the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (“ERISA”), as a plan maintained outside the United States primarily for the benefit of persons substantially all of whom are nonresident aliens of the United States. To preserve this exemption, both Active Membership in the Plan and the opportunity to increase Highest Average Monthly Earnings after ceasing to be an Active Member, as provided in Section 4.04(b), shall be limited to individuals who are nonresident aliens of the United States and whose assigned work locations are outside the United States, and all permanent records and documentation relating to the administration of the Plan shall be kept outside the United States. The Plan is also intended to be completely exempt from United States Internal Revenue Code section 409A (“Section 409A”), and shall be subject to the special operating rules and limitations in this Section 9.14, effective for any period to which Section 409A applies. It is intended that no Member who is a U.S. Person may have their benefit from the Plan vest, increase, or be enhanced (collectively, a “Benefit Enhancement”) as a result of their compensation or service while a U.S. Person. Therefore, no Member shall become entitled to a Benefit Enhancement with respect to a calendar year until it is determined, following the close of such year, that the Member was not a U.S. Person for such year. Notwithstanding, in the calendar year a Member’s benefit under the Plan is scheduled to commence, the Vice President may authorize a Benefit Enhancement for that year if they determine satisfactorily that the Member will not be a U.S. Person for such year. In all other cases, the Member’s benefit will commence without any Benefit Enhancement related to the calendar year of commencement, and appropriate adjustments will be made in the following year if it is determined that the Member was not a U.S. Person in that year. This Section 9.14 shall always be interpreted and applied in accordance with the overriding requirement that benefits and any other rights under the Plan must remain entirely exempt from Section 409A, and the Vice President shall have such unrestricted authority as necessary to ensure this requirement is met. The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DB Program document, as amended and restated, is adopted as of December 19, 2022, and is effective as of January 1, 2023 or as otherwise stated herein. The document is signed by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer of PepsiCo, Inc., on December 19, 2022, and approved by Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel, on December 9, 2022. Table A sets forth the formulas for calculating the Pension payable to a Member under Article IV or the Death Benefit payable to a Member’s Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner under Article VI, subject to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I. Any benefits accrued by a Member while a part-time employee, following designation by the Vice President as an Eligible Employee under Section 2.01, shall be prorated as determined by the Vice President to reflect the approximate ratio of the Member’s level of services during part-time status to the level required for full-time status at their work location. (I) Member’s Pension: For Members who became members before January 1, 1976, the Pension payable at Normal Retirement Date as a Single Life Annuity is the larger of (1) 1.5 percent of the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary multiplied by the number of years of Pensionable Service, or (2) 3 percent of the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary multiplied by the number of years of Pensionable Service, not exceeding 15 years. For Members who became members on or after January 1, 1976, and for persons who became members on or after September 1, 1980 (excluding those in the first group), and for persons who became members after November 12, 1998 (excluding those in the first two groups), the Pension is calculated as the aggregate of (1) 3 percent of the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary multiplied by the number of years of Pensionable Service, not exceeding 10 years, plus (2) 1 percent of the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary multiplied by the number of years of Pensionable Service in excess of 10. At the discretion of the Vice President, the Pension may be reduced by: (1) all state pension and social security benefits attributable to service other than those from unmatched and unreimbursed voluntary contributions by the Member; (2) the annuity equivalent of a like portion of all capital sum benefits from retirement due to local legislation or termination indemnities; (3) benefits from other retirement plans or cash allowances of the Employers for periods qualifying as Pensionable Service under both the DB Program and such other plans; (4) any severance payments made at termination due to a severance agreement; (5) the value (as determined by methodology approved by the Vice President) of any benefits paid prior to retirement from any plan for periods qualifying as Pensionable Service under both the DB Program and such other plans; and (6) any deductions, reductions, or forfeitures due to misdemeanor, misconduct, or discharge for cause under Section 9.08. No such deduction applies to benefits from unmatched and unreimbursed voluntary contributions by the Member. The value of all such deductions is subject to adjustment for form and timing of payment, and all deductions are calculated as of the Member’s termination date using a methodology approved by the Vice President. If the Pension is reduced under paragraph (c), an alternative calculation applies unless the Vice President determines it is unnecessary or impractical or fails to serve the purposes of the DB Program. Under this alternative calculation, only the Member’s Pensionable Service under the DB Program (excluding employment considered in paragraphs (c)(1)–(5)) is considered, and reductions under (c)(1)–(5) are disregarded (though the reduction under (c)(6) is taken into account). The Pension under this alternative calculation is compared to the Pension under (a), (b), and (c), and the greater amount is payable, subject to the remaining provisions of this paragraph (d). This alternative calculation is intended to replicate the effect of the “extended wearaway” methodology as in effect under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan. Notwithstanding, any benefit increase resulting from this paragraph (d) will be limited by the Vice President to not exceed what should be available given the intent described. For purposes of this Table A, “Highest Average Monthly Salary” means one twelfth of the yearly average of the Member’s Salary over any 5 consecutive calendar years of Service in which such Salary was highest (or a lesser period if the Member has been in Service less than 5 years). In determining the Highest Average Monthly Salary, a calendar year with no Salary is disregarded, and the preceding and following years are considered consecutive. If a calendar year includes an unpaid authorized leave or other absence from paid service resulting in less than a complete year of Salary, that year is disregarded and the next preceding or succeeding year or years are taken into account if it results in a higher average. In determining the amount of a Deferred Vested Pension under Section 4.04, the Pension shall be equal to the greatest of the amounts determined under (1), (2), or (3): (1) the Pension calculated under (b) based on Pensionable Service the Member would have earned had they remained an Active Member until their Normal Retirement Age (subject to a maximum of 35 years) and Highest Average Monthly Salary as of September 30, 2003, reduced by a fraction with numerator equal to the Member’s actual years of Pensionable Service prior to October 1, 2003 (subject to a maximum of 35 years) and denominator equal to the years of Pensionable Service they would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Age; (2) the aggregate of (i) the Pension calculated under (b) based on Pensionable Service the Member would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date and Highest Average Monthly Salary as of September 30, 2003, reduced by a fraction with numerator equal to the Member’s actual years of Pensionable Service prior to October 1, 2003 and denominator equal to the years of Pensionable Service they would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date; and (ii) the Pension calculated under (b) based on Pensionable Service the Member would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date and Highest Average Monthly Salary at the date the Member ceases to be in Service, reduced by a fraction with numerator equal to the Member’s actual years of Pensionable Service after September 30, 2003 and denominator equal to the years of Pensionable Service they would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date; (3) the Pension calculated under (b) based on Pensionable Service the Member would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date and Highest Average Monthly Salary at the date the Member ceases to be in Service, reduced by a fraction with numerator equal to the Member’s actual years of Pensionable Service and denominator equal to the years of Pensionable Service they would have earned had they remained an Active Member until Normal Retirement Date. For Members who became members before January 1, 1976, the Deferred Vested Pension shall be the larger of 1.5 percent of the Member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary multiplied by the Member’s number of years of Pensionable Service at termination or the amount determined by the Vice President based on actuarial information provided to the Vice President. All deductions set out in (c) that apply to a Member entitled to a Deferred Vested Pension are calculated as of the time such Member ceases to be in Service and in accordance with methodology approved by the Vice President. (II) Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension: If a Member covered by Section 6.01 dies after the date they would have been entitled to retire early under Section 4.02, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension shall be 50 percent of the Pension to which the Member would have been entitled if they had retired on the day preceding their death (having elected a 50 Percent Survivor Annuity under Section 5.02(b)) and reduced in accordance with Section 4.02 if the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner commences the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension prior to the date the Member would have attained age 62. If a Member covered by Section 6.01 dies before the date they would have been entitled to retire early under Section 4.02, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension shall be 50 percent of the Pension to which the Member would have been entitled if they had attained the right to receive a 50 Percent Survivor Annuity under Section 5.02(b)), payable as of the first of the month following the later of death or the date the Member would have attained age 55, and reduced in accordance with Section 4.04(c) if the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner commences the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension prior to the date the Member would have attained age 65. Appendix ERW supplements the main portion of the DB Program with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees. This section provides definitions for the following terms in boldface and underlined. Where they appear in this Appendix ERW with initial capitals, they have the meaning set forth below. Except as otherwise provided in this Appendix ERW, all defined terms shall have the meaning given to them in Section 2.01 of the DB Program. (a) Appendix ERW: This Appendix ERW to the DB Program. (b) Covered Employee: An Active Member who: (1) is an Eligible Employee of an Employer at the time their employment is terminated involuntarily pursuant to the Reorganization; and (2) (i) for purposes of the 2007/2008 Restructuring, has their last day of active employment between the Effective Date and December 31, 2008 (inclusive) and has.

This Appendix ERW supplements the main portion of the DB Program by outlining the rights and benefits of Covered Employees related to early retirement. A Covered Employee is an Active Member who (1) is an Eligible Employee of an Employer at the time of involuntary termination due to the Reorganization; (2) for the 2007/2008 Restructuring, has their last day of active employment between the Effective Date and December 31, 2008 (inclusive), with a Severance Date on or after the Effective Date but no later than December 31, 2009; or for the 2008/2009 Restructuring, has their last day of active employment between the Effective Date and August 31, 2009 (inclusive), with a Severance Date on or after the Effective Date but no later than December 26, 2009; (3) is entitled to enhanced severance pay under the Severance Program as part of the Reorganization or to severance pay under an agreement described in (5); (4) is authorized in writing by the Vice President to receive benefits under this Appendix ERW; and (5) signs, submits, and does not revoke a qualifying severance agreement that releases the Corporation and the Associated Companies and their employees, agents, and affiliates from liability, subject to the Corporation’s determination that (i) the agreement meets all substance, form, and timing requirements applied by the Corporation and (ii) it is entered into under the Severance Program as part of the Reorganization. Any Active Member who does not meet all of these requirements is not a Covered Employee and is not eligible for benefits under this Appendix ERW. The Reorganization refers to the reorganization, plant closing, or other event that triggered the applicable Severance Program. The Severance Date is an Active Member’s final day of employment with the Employer pursuant to the Reorganization. For the 2007/2008 Restructuring, the Severance Program includes both the “PepsiCo Transition Severance Program for the 2007 Restructuring for Salaried Employees Below Band 1” and the “PepsiCo Transition Severance Program for the Equipment & Service Management Restructuring for Salaried Employees below Band 1,” with an Effective Date of February 4, 2008. For the 2008/2009 Restructuring, the Severance Program includes both the “PepsiCo Transition Severance Program for the 2008/2009 Restructuring for Salaried Employees Below Band I” and the “PepsiCo Transition Severance Program for the 2008/2009 Restructuring for Salaried Employees Band I,” with an Effective Date of April 3, 2009. Any Covered Employee who meets the eligibility requirements under subsection (a) is treated as eligible for a Special Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.03. To be eligible, an individual must (1) be a Covered Employee on their Severance Date; (2) for the 2007/2008 Restructuring only, have attained at least age 50 (but not age 55) by their Severance Date and be credited with at least 10 years of Vesting Service as of their Severance Date; (3) for the 2008/2009 Restructuring only, have attained at least age 50 (but not age 55) by their “Pension Termination Date” (the earlier of the Severance Date or 52 weeks after the last day of active employment pursuant to the Reorganization), be credited with at least 10 years of Vesting Service as of their Severance Date, not return to employment with an Employer before their Pension Termination Date, and not be otherwise eligible for Normal or Early Retirement Pension. For age and service requirements, the Covered Member’s age and years of Vesting Service are rounded up to the nearest whole year. The amount of the Special Early Retirement Pension is reduced by 4/12ths of 1 percent per month as per Section 4.03, and is subject to all usual limitations in the DB Program. The Special Early Retirement Pension under this Appendix ERW is in lieu of the Special Early Retirement Pension under Rule 4.03 of the DB Program, and Covered Employees are not entitled to or receive such a pension under Section 4.03. Additionally, the Special Early Retirement Pension under this Appendix ERW is not available to individuals eligible for special early retirement under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan unless a release of such claim acceptable to the Corporation is provided. By accepting benefits under this Appendix ERW, a Covered Employee is conclusively presumed to have irrevocably waived any right to a Special Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.03 or to special early retirement benefits under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan or any other plan maintained or contributed to by the Corporation or an Associated Company. Any Covered Employee treated as eligible for an Early Retirement Pension under this Rule ERW is also deemed to qualify for “Retirement” for purposes of their outstanding stock option and restricted stock unit awards under the PepsiCo Inc. Long-Term Incentive Plan, the PepsiCo, Inc. 2003 Long-Term Incentive Plan, the PepsiCo, Inc. 1994 Long-Term Incentive Plan, the PepsiCo, Inc. 1995 Stock Option Incentive Plan, and the PepsiCo SharePower Stock Option Plan. The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC) was amended and restated effective January 1, 2022. The Plan was first established in September 1980, amended and restated in September 1982, and again in October 2003, when the Plan Rules became the “Plan A Rules” and “Plan B Rules.” On January 1, 2005, it was amended to ensure that no person subject to U.S. taxation has their right to a benefit enhanced, instead being treated as if they had permanently left the Corporation and Associated Companies before becoming subject to U.S. taxation. On January 1, 2010, the Plan A Rules and Plan B Rules were combined into one document, which remains in effect and is referred to as the “DB Program.” On January 1, 2011, a new defined contribution structure (the DC Program) was established for selected international employees, including those on assignments outside their home countries and certain senior globalists on U.S. tax equalized packages. The DC Program was amended and restated on January 1, 2016 to include selected employees localized outside their home countries who were previously participating in a defined benefit or defined contribution program and for whom no company-provided retirement program is available. On January 1, 2019, the DC Program was amended to recognize same-sex and opposite-sex domestic partners for certain purposes for Members actively employed or on authorized leave of absence on or after January 1, 2019. It was again amended and restated on January 1, 2021. The DC Program is now amended and restated effective January 1, 2022. The Plan is unfunded and unsecured under U.S. Internal Revenue Code and ERISA, and benefits are considered obligations of the individual employer, with the executive having the rights of an unsecured general creditor. The Plan is also intended to be exempt from ERISA as a plan maintained outside the United States primarily for the benefit of nonresident aliens. In the DC Program, an “Approved Transfer” includes a transfer to employment in the United States or its territories, a secondment to a U.S. work location, or any other change in employment circumstances that makes the Member a U.S. Person, initiated or approved by the Corporation or with Corporation approval by the Member’s Employer. An “Associated Company” is any company or undertaking directly or indirectly controlled by or associated in business with the Corporation and that has agreed, subject to the Vice President’s ongoing consent, to perform and observe the conditions, stipulations, and provisions of the DC Program and be included among the Employers under the DC Program. The “Corporation” means PepsiCo, Inc., a corporation organized under the laws of North Carolina, or its successor. A “Dependant” is the person who receives the balance of a Member’s PIRP-DC Account upon the Member’s death. The “DB Program” refers to the defined benefits portion of the Plan as described in the governing legal document “The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Benefit Program (PIRP DB), as it may be amended from time to time,” also referred to as “PIRP-DB.” The “DC Program” refers to the defined contributions portion of the Plan as described in the governing legal document “The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), as it may be amended from time to time,” also referred to as “PIRP-DC.” The “Distribution Valuation Date” is the date specified by the Vice President for valuing PIRP-DC Accounts for distributions under Article VI; currently, it is the month end immediately following the event triggering distribution, so if the trigger occurs on December 30, the valuation date is December 31, and if on December 31, it is January 31 of the following year. The Vice President may change any current Distribution Valuation Date, and values are determined at the close of that date or, if not a business day, the close of the preceding business day. The “Effective Date” for the DC Program is January 1, 2011. An “Eligible Domestic Partner” is an individual of the same sex or opposite sex as the Member who is actively employed by or on an Authorized Leave of Absence from a member of the PepsiCo Organization on or after January 1, 2019, and who satisfies one of the following conditions: (1) has entered into a civil union or similar government-recognized status valid at the Member’s death under the law of the Member’s principal residence, with the individual submitting a claim for benefits within 60 days of the Member’s date of death.

The “Effective Date” is defined as January 1, 2011. An “Eligible Domestic Partner” applies only to a Member who is actively employed by or on an authorized leave of absence from a member of the PepsiCo Organization on or after January 1, 2019, and must be of the same sex or opposite sex as the Member, satisfying one of the following conditions as determined by the Vice President: (1) a civil union or similar government-recognized status valid at the Member’s death under the law of the Member’s principal residence, with the individual’s claim for benefits submitted within 60 days of the Member’s death; (2) enrollment in the Cigna International Health Program (or its successor) as the Member’s domestic partner on the applicable date; or (3) meeting criteria specified in writing by the Vice President, with a claim for benefits submitted within 60 days of the Member’s death. The term “Eligible Domestic Partner” does not apply to a Member’s Eligible Spouse, and a Member may not have more than one Eligible Domestic Partner at any time, nor may a Member with an Eligible Spouse have an Eligible Domestic Partner. An “Eligible Employee” is someone the Vice President determines is employed exclusively outside the United States on a full-time salaried basis with an Approved Employer, is not actively accruing or designated to accrue benefits under the DB Program, and meets at least one of the following: (1) is on an assignment outside his home country where it is impractical to participate in retirement plans in his home country; (2) is on his second or more consecutive assignment outside his home country (effective January 1, 2021), and retirement plans in his home country do not include those sponsored by the Corporation or an Affiliated Company; (3) is among a selected group of senior globalists on U.S. tax equalized packages whose positions and employment terms the Vice President has determined make them eligible for the DC Program; or (4) is localized to a country outside his home country, was actively participating in a retirement program sponsored by a PepsiCo Organization member prior to localization, and the local employer does not sponsor a retirement plan. The Vice President may designate part-time employees as Eligible Employees if, but for their part-time status, they meet all requirements. An “Eligible Spouse” is the individual to whom the Member is married or was married on the date of death, with the determination of marriage based on the law of the Member’s principal residence, and a Member shall have only one Eligible Spouse. “Employers” include the Corporation and any Associated Company, with “Approved Employer” meaning an Employer approved by the Vice President to allow its Eligible Employees to become and remain Active Members. The “Entry Date” is the date the Vice President specifies for an Eligible Employee’s admission to Membership. An “Interest Credit” is the annual credit to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account under Section 4.01(b). The “Interest Rate” is the annualized rate of interest on 30-year Treasury securities as prescribed by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service for the month of September immediately preceding the first day of the Plan Year to which the Interest Credit relates, and the Vice President may change the basis for determining the Interest Rate as needed to ensure it is readily determinable and administrable, and does not exceed a level considered earnings under Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(o). A “Member” is an Eligible Employee admitted to Membership under Article III and who remains entitled to benefits under the DC Program, with references to “Membership” indicating the status of being a Member, and “Active Member” and “Inactive Member” having the respective meanings in Section 3.03. A “Pay Credit” is the credit made to an Active Member’s PIRP-DC Account under Section 4.01(a). The “Plan” is the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, consisting of the DC Program and DB Program. A “Plan Year” is a 12-consecutive-month period beginning January 1 and ending December 31 of the same calendar year. The “PepsiCo Organization” is the controlled group of organizations of which the Corporation is a part, as defined by U.S. Internal Revenue Code section 414 and regulations thereunder. A “PIRP-DC Account” is an unfunded, notional account maintained for a Member on the books of the Member’s Employer to indicate the dollar amount credited under the DC Program, with the balance determined by interpretive principles and decisions applied by the Vice President. “Salary” means (i) home notional base salary for an Eligible Employee not paid on a U.S. payroll, and (ii) base salary plus annual bonus for an Eligible Employee paid on a U.S. payroll, with the exception that for Eligible Employees not paid on a U.S. payroll who become Active Members on or after January 1, 2021, Salary includes home notional base salary plus annual bonus. The Vice President determines Salary and has the authority to increase it to reflect a notional bonus for employees in countries other than the United States, and such determination is conclusive and binding. “Service” is the period of continuous employment with any Approved Employer, including authorized leaves of absence of not more than 12 months unless individually authorized in writing by the Vice President; a “Break in Service” is a period not in employment with any Approved Employer, which is counted as Service only if it lasts no more than 12 months unless individually authorized; pre-transfer employment with an Employer before a Break in Service may be counted as Service only with Vice President approval, and post-transfer employment after a transfer from an Approved Employer to another Employer may be counted as Service only with Vice President approval; Service does not include periods of employment prior to an entity becoming an Employer or a member of the PepsiCo Organization. A “Status Change” is any change in a Member’s circumstances (other than an Approved Transfer) that causes the Member to become a U.S. Person. A “U.S. Person” is (1) a U.S. citizen; (2) a person lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the U.S. at any time during the calendar year or who has applied for such residence; or (3) a resident alien under U.S. Internal Revenue Code section 7701(b)(1)(A), including those meeting the substantial presence test or making an election to be treated as a U.S. resident; additionally, a person is considered a U.S. Person for Section 9.14 if required to file a U.S. individual income tax return, unless the Vice President determines there is no U.S. source earned income from a PepsiCo Organization member. A “Valuation date” is each business day as determined by the Vice President, as of which Members’ PIRP-DC Accounts are valued (except for distributions under Article VI), with the Valuation Date for all Members as of the last day of each Plan Year as of the Effective Date, and a special Valuation Date prior to the end of a Plan Year for Active Members with an Approved Transfer or a Status Change, as described in Section 4.02; any current Valuation Date may be changed by the Vice President, with adjustments applied to prevent duplicate or disproportionate benefits; values are determined as of the close of a Valuation Date or, if not a business day, as of the close of the preceding business day. The “Vice President” is the Vice President, Global Benefits & Wellness of PepsiCo, Inc., and if that position is vacant or eliminated, it shall be the person acting to fulfill the majority of the duties (or plurality if no one fulfills a majority) as they existed immediately prior to the vacancy or elimination. Under Article III, every person determined by the Vice President to be an Eligible Employee is eligible for Membership. Every Eligible Employee who is not a U.S. Person during the relevant time shall be admitted to Membership following Vice President approval, effective as of the Entry Date, with the relevant time including a sufficient period before the Proposed Entry Date to avoid the PIRP-DC Account being considered deferred compensation subject to Section 409A of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code; no person shall be admitted to Membership without Vice President approval. A Member is an Active Member during the period they are (a) employed as an Eligible Employee, (b) not a U.S. Person, and (c) currently approved by the Vice President as an Active Member; otherwise, they are an Inactive Member. Under Section 4.01, the Employer allocates Pay Credits and Interest Credits to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account, with the Pay Credit determined by multiplying the Active Member’s annualized Salary in effect as of the Valuation Date by the Member’s applicable percentage—5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%—for Active Members who become Active Members on or after January 1, 2021 and have no Service completed while a U.S. Person, the Pay Credit is determined by the number of “points” based on the sum of the Member’s age and years of Service, each expressed in whole years and days, with the following point ranges: less than 35 (5% of Eligible Pay), 35–39 (6%), 40–44 (7%), 45–49 (8%), 50–54 (9%), 55–59 (10%), 60–64 (11%), 65 or more (12%).

The amount of an Active Member’s Pay Credit is determined by their applicable percentage, which is one of 5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%, based on the number of “points” calculated as the sum of the Member’s age and years of Service, each expressed in whole years and days. For an Eligible Employee who becomes an Active Member on or after January 1, 2021 and has no Service completed while a U.S. Person, the Pay Credit is determined by the following points ranges: less than 35 points equals 5% of Eligible Pay; 35–39 points equals 6%; 40–44 points equals 7%; 45–49 points equals 8%; 50–54 points equals 9%; 55–59 points equals 10%; 60–64 points equals 11%; 65 or more points equals 12%. Otherwise, the Vice President specifies the applicable percentage as of the Active Member’s Entry Date (or, if the Member ceases and then becomes an Active Member again, as of the date they re-enter). For each subsequent Plan Year, the Vice President may specify a new applicable percentage, which applies to that Plan Year. Pay Credits are prorated if the Member has less than one full year of Active Membership during a Plan Year, with the fractional year calculated by dividing the Member’s days of Active Membership by the total days in the Plan Year. A period of paid leave is considered Active Membership for Pay Credit purposes, but unpaid leave is not, and thus Pay Credits are prorated or eliminated for the year containing unpaid leave. In the Member’s final year of Membership, Pay Credits and Interest Credits are determined as of the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date, with proration based on the fractional final year. The Vice President determines Pay Credits and Interest Credits as soon as administratively practicable after each Valuation Date, and these determinations are conclusive and binding. An Interest Credit is available if the Member is an Active or Inactive Member during a Plan Year and has a balance in their PIRP-DC Account as of the prior Valuation Date; the amount is calculated by multiplying the Interest Rate for the period since the last Valuation Date by the balance in the Account as of that date. Interest Credits are also prorated if the Member has less than one full year of Membership since the last Valuation Date. Offsets may reduce any payment or benefit by the amount of any obligation to the Corporation or by (a) material benefits accrued under a retirement plan sponsored by the Corporation or a political subdivision, to the extent the Vice President determines the benefit relates to Service or Salary considered in Pay Credits, and (b) termination indemnity or other payments related to termination of employment, to the extent the Vice President determines the payment is reasonably related to Service considered in Pay Credits. These offsets may apply to Pay Credits, Interest Credits, the PIRP-DC Account balance, or distributions. The Vice President has sole discretion in determining whether a benefit is material and in applying this Section. Pay Credits and Interest Credits are credited to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account as of the Valuation Date (or the Distribution Valuation Date in the final year of Membership) or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter. The PIRP-DC Account is a bookkeeping device to track the notional value of Pay Credits and Interest Credits and the Employer’s liability, with no assets reserved, funded, insured, or secured. A Member becomes fully vested in their PIRP-DC Account after completing 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed, with disability determined by the Vice President using standards deemed appropriate. Special vesting applies automatically to an Active Member with an Approved Transfer as of the last business day before the earlier of the transfer or the date they become a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer. For a Status Change, the Member may request special vesting as of the last business day before the change, but the request and Vice President’s approval must be final and in place prior to the date of application. The effect of special vesting is that the Member becomes vested to the same extent as under Section 5.02, subject to the requirement that allocations, benefits, and rights remain exempt from Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. Distributions from the PIRP-DC Account are made in a single lump sum upon termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, whichever occurs first, and are made on the first day of the month following the Distribution Valuation Date. For a disabled termination, the Vice President determines disability and the termination date. Upon death, distributions are made to the Member’s Dependant; if no Dependant is designated or all designated dependants predeceased the Member, the distribution goes to the Member’s Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or to the estate if neither exists. The PIRP-DC Account continues to be credited with Interest Credits and debited for expenses until the Distribution Valuation Date. A Member may designate one or more dependants in writing on forms provided by the Vice President, and may change or revoke the designation at any time before the effective date, with written consent of the Eligible Spouse required for designating a non-spouse dependent. Revocation does not require spouse consent. Designations and changes must be filed with the Vice President to be effective. The Plan is administered by the Vice President, who has sole authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, and make all determinations, which are final and binding. The Vice President may delegate responsibilities to others, and any reference to the Vice President may refer to a delegate. If a person entitled to a benefit is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the person’s benefit, which constitutes a complete discharge of liability. The Vice President has exclusive discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility, and decide benefit amounts, with all decisions final and conclusive. This discretion is absolute, even if not expressly granted or required by the Plan, and is intended to be maximal. Decisions are subject to review by a court, arbitrator, or tribunal under the arbitrary and capricious standard. If a claim is denied, the Vice President or a designated party provides a written notice within 90 days that includes the reason for denial, references to relevant Plan provisions, information needed to perfect the claim, and a description of the claim review process. If special circumstances require an extension, the period may be extended to 180 days, with notice given before the 90-day period ends. Upon review, the claimant is given the opportunity to submit comments, documents, and records, which are considered regardless of whether they were previously considered. The review decision is made within 60 days, or up to an additional 60 days if extended, with notice given before the initial 60-day period ends. The final decision is in writing, clearly explained, includes specific reasons and references to Plan provisions, and provides the claimant free access to all relevant documents and records upon request. Any claim reviewed by a court, arbitrator, or tribunal is based solely on the record before the Vice President at the time of the original determination and is subject to the claimant having fully exhausted all rights under this section and Section 7.07. Any claim or action for alleged wrongful denial of benefits must be filed within two years of when the cause of action first accrues. For purposes of this subsection, a cause of action accrues not later than the date of the denial.

Any claim under the Plan reviewed by a court, arbitrator, or other tribunal shall be based solely on the record before the Vice President at the time of their initial determination and shall only proceed if the claimant has fully exhausted all rights under Section 7.03 and in accordance with Section 7.07. A claim for alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits must be filed within two years of when the cause of action first accrues, which is deemed to occur not later than the earlier of (i) when the claimant receives the calculation of the benefits in question, (ii) the date identified by the Vice President when payments are to commence, or (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts supporting the claim. Failure to file within this two-year period will bar the claimant or their representative from pursuing it, and correspondence or communications after the mandatory appeals process will not extend this time limit. Any claim or action related to the Plan must be brought only in the state or federal courts of New York, specifically the one nearest the Corporation’s headquarters. Specific references in the Plan to the Vice President’s discretion do not imply that their discretion in any other context is narrower or less broad. Before filing a claim, suit, or action in court or another tribunal, a claimant must fully exhaust all rights under the claims procedure in Section 7.03. Exhaustion is intended to apply in all circumstances, including for failure to respond to a claim unless the claimant made it reasonably clear to the Vice President that they were submitting a claim, or for failure to request documents unless (A) the Plan or applicable law requires them, (B) the request is in writing and addressed to and received by the Vice President, (C) the Vice President fails to provide the documents within six months of receipt or a reasonable longer period, and (D) the requestor made it reasonably clear they were asserting a legal right to the documents. A person not treated as a Member is not deemed to have taken sufficient steps unless they clearly communicate to the Vice President their entitlement as a Member. The exhaustion requirement applies regardless of whether other disputes are more significant, to any rights the Vice President may provide, whether actual or potential, and even if no specific procedures exist for the dispute, in which case the Vice President must either establish procedures or apply those in Section 7.03. The Vice President may make special arrangements to consider claims on a class basis or address unusual conflicts, but such arrangements must ensure exhaustion is required to the maximum extent. A “Dispute” includes any claim, issue, assertion, or matter, and a “Claim” is any Dispute that involves (A) the interpretation of the Plan, (B) any term or condition of the Plan, (C) the interpretation of the Plan in light of applicable law, (D) whether the Plan has been validly adopted, (E) the administration of the Plan, (F) whether the Plan has violated applicable law or regulation, (G) a request for or attempt to recover benefits, (H) an assertion of a legal duty, or (I) any claim deemed similar by the Vice President or relating to the Plan. A “Claimant” includes any actual or putative Eligible Employee, former Employee, Member, former Member, Dependant, or their spouse, former spouse, estate, heir, or representative, or any other individual, person, or entity with a relationship to such individuals or the Plan, or a group of such individuals. The Corporation reserves the right to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time, but no such amendment or termination may reduce the balance in a Member’s Plan account (as of the date of amendment or termination) except to the extent the Member becomes entitled to an amount under another employer’s plan. Specific forms or times of payment are not protected. The Corporation may amend the Plan at its sole discretion, with or without retroactive effect, but no Employer other than the Corporation may amend the Plan. If the Plan is terminated with respect to fewer than all Employers, it continues for the benefit of employees of the remaining Employers. The Employers’ obligations under the Plan are unfunded and constitute liabilities payable from their general funds, and rights to benefits are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors. All costs and expenses of the Plan are borne by the Employers and are allocated based on the proportion of Members employed by each Employer. If a Member is absent from duty for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation), they are deemed to have terminated employment 12 months after the absence begins, unless the Vice President determines otherwise. If the absence is due to full-time service in the armed forces or national service, the Member is not deemed to have terminated employment as long as they are regarded as remaining employed or until they resign permanently, whichever occurs first. If the Vice President determines that a Member engaged in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of their termination, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits, and their PIRP-DC Account is adjusted to reflect the forfeiture, with previously paid credits being recovered. Prohibited Misconduct includes (1) accepting employment or ownership in a business that markets, sells, distributes, or produces “Covered Products” unless it makes retail sales or consumes such products without competing with PepsiCo, (2) soliciting a PepsiCo employee to leave or join another entity, (3) using or disclosing confidential information about PepsiCo’s customers, suppliers, distributors, operations, products, pricing, processes, research, financial data, or strategies, (4) engaging in acts contrary to PepsiCo’s best interests, including violating the Code of Conduct, unlawful trading based on PepsiCo information, or gross misconduct, or (5) engaging in fraud. Notwithstanding these provisions, a Member may communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations without notice, participate in investigations, or receive awards for such disclosures, and the Corporation retains its attorney-client privilege. Under the Defend Trade Secrets Act, a person is not liable for disclosing a trade secret to a government official or attorney for reporting or investigating suspected violations, or in a sealed complaint, and may use trade secret information in court proceedings if the document is filed under seal and the trade secret is not disclosed except pursuant to court order. “Participation” includes serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor, providing input, advice, guidance, or recommendations, or giving a testimonial on behalf of a business entity. “Covered Products” means any product.
