If a Participant’s period of Service (as so determined) would extend beyond the Participant’s Separation from Service date because of an authorized leave of absence related to a Company severance program or agreement, the Plan Administrator may provide for determining the Participant’s 409A Pension at Separation from Service by projecting the benefit the Participant would have if all such Service were taken into account under the Plan. 3.3 Credited Service: Subject to the next two sentences, the amount of a Participant’s Pension, Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension shall be based upon the Participant’s period of Credited Service, as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan. (a) Inpats. Any provision in Section 3.5 of Part B of the Salaried Plan which resulted in disregarding the pre-transfer Credited Service of certain inpats who transferred to the United States shall not apply under this Plan in the case of such inpats who transfer to the United States before October 1, 2014, unless such earlier application avoids duplication of benefits under the Salaried Plan. (b) Leaves of Absence. If a Participant’s period of Credited Service (as so determined) would extend beyond the Participant’s Separation from Service date because of an authorized leave of absence related to a Company severance program or agreement, the Plan Administrator may provide for determining the Participant’s 409A Pension at Separation from Service by projecting the benefit the Participant would have if all such Service were taken into account under the Plan. ARTICLE IV Requirements for Benefits A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner, as applicable, shall be eligible for certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article. The amount of any such Pension or survivor benefit shall be determined in accordance with Article V. 4.1 Normal 409A Retirement Pension: A Participant shall be eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement Pension if he Separates from Service after attaining Normal Retirement Age. 4.2 Early 409A Retirement Pension: A Participant shall be eligible for an Early 409A Retirement Pension if he Separates from Service prior to attaining Normal Retirement Age but after attaining at least age 55 and completing 10 or more years of Elapsed Time Service. 4.3 409A Vested Pension: A Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 shall be eligible to receive a 409A Vested Pension if he Separates from Service before he is eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement Pension or an Early 409A Retirement Pension. A Participant who terminates employment prior to satisfying the vesting requirement in Section 4.7 shall not be eligible to receive a Pension under this Plan. 4.4 Late 409A Retirement Pension: A Participant who continues without a Separation from Service after his Normal Retirement Age shall not receive a Pension until his Late Retirement Date. Thereafter, a Participant shall be eligible for a Late Retirement Pension determined in accordance with Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (but without regard to any requirement for notice of suspension under ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) or any adjustment as under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan). 4.5 409A Disability Pension: A Participant shall be eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if he meets the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan. A Participant’s 409A Disability Pension, if any, shall generally be comprised of two parts. The first part shall represent the benefits with respect to a disabled Participant’s Credited Service through the day of the Participant’s Separation from Service (i.e., the Participant’s “Pre-Separation Accruals”). In the event the disabled Participant continues to receive Credited Service related to the disability after such Separation from Service, the Participant’s 409A Disability Pension shall have a second part, which shall represent all benefits accrued with respect to Credited Service from the date immediately following the Participant’s Separation from Service until the earliest of the Participant’s (i) attainment of age 65, (ii) benefit commencement date under Part B of the Salaried Plan or (iii) recovery from the disability (i.e., the Participant’s “Post-LTD Accruals”). 4.6 Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is payable under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date. Any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension payable on behalf of a Participant shall commence as of the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s death and, (ii) the date the Participant attains or would have attained age 55. Subject to Section 4.9, any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension shall continue monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse. (a) Active, Disabled and Retired Employees: A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension shall be payable under this subsection to a Participant’s Eligible Spouse (if any) who is entitled under Part B of the Salaried Plan to the pre-retirement spouse’s pension for survivors of active, disabled and retired employees. The amount (if any) of such Pension shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Section 5.3.

A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is payable only if the Participant dies prior to their Annuity Starting Date. Such a pension commences on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s death and (ii) the date the Participant attains or would have attained age 55. It continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse, subject to Section 4.9. For active, disabled, and retired employees, the pension is payable to an Eligible Spouse entitled under Part B of the Salaried Plan to the pre-retirement spouse’s pension for survivors, with the amount determined under Section 5.3 after applying Section 5.6. For vested terminated employees, the pension is payable to an Eligible Spouse entitled under Part B of the Salaried Plan to the pre-retirement spouse’s pension for survivors of vested terminated employees, also determined under Section 5.3 after Section 5.6. If such coverage is in effect, the Pension calculated under Section 5.2(b) is reduced annually by a percentage based on the Participant’s age at the time of coverage, as follows: up to 35 years – 0.0%, 35–39 – 0.075%, 40–44 – 0.1%, 45–49 – 0.175%, 50–54 – 0.3%, 55–59 – 0.5%, 60–64 – 0.5%, with a pro rata reduction for partial years. No reduction applies for coverage within 90 days of termination. A Participant is fully vested in their Accrued Benefit at the time they become fully vested under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A). The distribution of a Participant’s 409A Pension begins as specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6. Any interest increase due to a delay in payment under Section 3.1(e) of Part A of the Salaried Plan accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the 409A Pension. Interest for delays caused by the Participant or prohibited by an IRS compliance correction program under Code section 409A is not allowed. For certain small benefit annuity payments, if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value of the 409A Pension at the Annuity Starting Date is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator distributes the lump sum. For Annuity Starting Dates prior to December 1, 2012, a Participant is cashed out if the Actuarial Equivalent value of their PEP Pension is equal to or less than $15,000. Similarly, for an Eligible Spouse, if the value of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit at the time payments commence, the lump sum is distributed; prior to December 1, 2012, this applies if the value is $15,000 or less. The Plan Administrator has discretion to cash out a 409A Vested Pension in a single lump sum if, as of December 1, 2012, the pension has not yet begun, its Actuarial Equivalent value is at or below the Cashout Limit, and it is practicable to calculate and distribute, with the cashout made on December 1, 2012. For any month in 2013 or later, as specified by the Plan Administrator, the same conditions apply, with the cashout made on the first day of that month. The Plan Administrator must memorialize such discretion in writing no later than November 30 for December 1, 2012, and no later than the day before the specified date for later years. For a Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner, if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value of the 409A Pension is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit at the time payments commence, the value is distributed; prior to December 1, 2012, if the value is $15,000 or less. Effective January 1, 2018, cashouts are not available for a Participant eligible for a “PEP Kicker” or a “Qualified Kicker” under a “Severance Program,” with these terms defined in Appendix Article E. Any lump sum distributed under this section replaces the otherwise distributable pension. The cashout provisions are considered “limited cashouts” under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v), and the entire accountable benefit—defined as the Participant’s total benefit under this Plan and all other nonaccount balance plans subject to Section 409A—must be cashed out at the time of payout. A cashout does not cause an accountable benefit to be paid before completing any applicable six-month delay (e.g., Section 6.6). No Participant, Eligible Spouse, or Eligible Domestic Partner may make a direct or indirect election regarding whether their Vested Pension, Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension, or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension will be cashed out. If a current or former Participant re-employs after receiving their Pension as an Annuity and is eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan, their 409A Pension continues in the same form as before re-employment, and any additional 409A Pension earned is based on the separation from service following re-employment. Effective beginning with benefits accrued after December 31, 2008 (“Post-2008 Accruals”), if a Participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of their Separation from Service, they forfeit all Post-2008 Accruals, and their 409A Pension is adjusted to reflect the forfeiture, with previously paid Post-2008 Accruals recovered. A Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension is payable only if the Participant dies prior to their Annuity Starting Date under either the 409A or Pre-409A Program. It commences on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s death and (ii) the date the Participant attains or would have attained age 55, and continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Domestic Partner, subject to Section 4.9. For active, disabled, and retired employees, the pension is payable to an Eligible Domestic Partner entitled under Part B of the Salaried Plan to the pre-retirement domestic partner’s pension for survivors, with the amount determined under Section 5.8 after applying Section 5.6. For vested terminated employees, the pension is payable to an Eligible Domestic Partner entitled under Part B of the Salaried Plan to the pre-retirement domestic partner’s pension for survivors of vested terminated employees, also determined under Section 5.8 after Section 5.6. If such coverage is in effect, the Pension calculated under Section 5.2(b) is reduced annually by the same percentages based on the Participant’s age: up to 35 – 0.0%, 35–39 – 0.075%, 40–44 – 0.1%, 45–49 – 0.175%, 50–54 – 0.3%, 55–59 – 0.5%, 60–64 – 0.5%, with a pro rata reduction for partial years. No reduction applies for coverage within 180 days of termination. The amount of a 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever applies), subject to adjustments under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and the Plan freeze described in Article I. A Participant’s 409A Pension is calculated by first determining their Total Pension, then subtracting their Salaried Plan Pension and further reducing by their Pre-409A Pension (but not below zero), with adjustments for early or late commencement, relative value of payment forms, and actuarial equivalents, as authorized by the Plan Administrator, including eliminating benefit duplication and, effective after December 31, 2018, providing makeup for early commencement reductions applied to the Pre-409A Pension that exceed those under the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, including any portion derived from the PEP Guarantee. The definitions in subsection (c) apply, where “Total Pension” means the greater of (i) the amount of the Participant’s pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations imposed by sections.

The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program includes rules authorized by the Plan Administrator to account for the time and form of prior payments and to eliminate all duplication of benefits. For annuity starting dates after December 31, 2018, a Participant’s 409A Pension may provide a makeup benefit to offset early commencement reduction factors applied to their Pre-409A Pension, where such reductions are greater than those under the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, including for portions of the Pre-409A Pension derived from the PEP Guarantee. A Participant’s “Total Pension” is the greater of (i) the amount of their pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or the actuarial adjustment in Section 5.7(d) of Part B, or (ii) the amount of their PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2, with the comparison adjusted for the relative value of payment forms. A “Salaried Plan Pension” is the amount under Part B of the Salaried Plan, and a “Pre-409A Pension” is the amount under Section 5.6. A Participant is eligible for a PEP Guarantee if they have at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings, defined as remuneration for the 1988 calendar year under the Salaried Plan as in effect in 1988, excluding remuneration from entities not then acting as Employers. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined using Formula A or B, with Formula A providing 3% of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1% for each year beyond 10, less 1-2/3% of the Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30, and for a Vested Pension, this is reduced by a fraction with the numerator as actual years of Credited Service and the denominator as years earned had the Participant remained employed until Normal Retirement Age. Formula B provides the greater of (A) 1-1/2% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service less 50% of the Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years up to 15 less 50% of the Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions, calculations are based on Credited Service, Highest Average Monthly Earnings, and Primary Social Security Amount at the date of disability. Special rules apply: if a Participant receives an Early Retirement Pension, the amount is reduced by 3/12ths of 1 percent per month before Normal Retirement Date; if entitled to a Vested Pension, the amount is reduced to the actuarial equivalent of the Normal Retirement Date amount if payment starts early, with Section 4.6(b) and 4.12(b) reductions applying; if the Participant receives a survivor annuity for a beneficiary other than an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner, the Pension is reduced to the actuarial equivalent of a Single Life Annuity; if the Pension includes inflation protection under Section 6.2(b), it is reduced to the actuarial equivalent of the annuity without such protection; and if the Pension is distributed as a lump sum, the amount is the actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, considering survivor benefits and early retirement reductions. For a surviving Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner, a survivor annuity equal to 50 percent of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee annuity is payable, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’s death and ending with the last monthly payment prior to the surviving spouse’s or partner’s death, with reductions of 0.8 percent per full year the spouse is more than 10 but less than 21 years younger, and an additional 0.4 percent per full year over 20 years younger. Pensions are subject to adjustments under this section, with “specified plan” meaning the Salaried Plan or a nonqualified pension plan sponsored by a PepsiCo Organization member and not based on participant pay deferrals. For rehired Participants, if their Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated due to additional Credited Service, their PEP Pension is recalculated to the maximum extent permissible under Section 409A, adjusting for in-service and prior distributions in the same manner as the Salaried Plan, but considering benefits under this Plan and any specified plans. If a benefit under a specified plan increases after PEP benefits are determined, the PEP benefit is recalculated to the maximum extent under Section 409A, and any overpayment is recovered as deemed appropriate. There is no duplication of payments under this Plan and any specified plans to the maximum extent under Section 409A. Effective January 1, 2009, if a Participant has earned a benefit under a “qualifying plan” under the “Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.8 of Part A of the Salaried Plan or the “Transfers and Non-Duplication” rule, no benefit offsets are allowed that would violate Section 409A. The monthly amount of a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is determined by first calculating the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (the greater of the Salaried Plan pension without Code limitations or actuarial adjustments or the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension), then reducing it by the Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, and further reducing it (but not below zero) by the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program, with adjustments for early or late commencement and actuarial equivalents under Plan Administrator rules. The Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is calculated as if payable at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, and the resulting amount is adjusted for commencement before or after that date. The Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the amount under the Salaried Plan, and the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program is the amount under the Pre-409A Program. The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is determined under either (1) the Normal Rule, which calculates the survivor annuity under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant had separated on the date of death (or earlier separation), commenced the annuity on the same date as the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s pension commencement, and died the day after commencement, or (2) the Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees, which ensures the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is at least 25 percent of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee, with Credited Service determined under Section 3.3(c)(2) of Part B of the Salaried Plan and the deceased Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation determined as of death, with no reduction for early commencement. Principles from Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) apply in determining the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension.

If a Participant’s plan benefit on their behalf is increased after PEP benefits have been determined—whether by court order, agreement with the plan administrator, or otherwise—the PEP benefit for the Participant must be recalculated to the maximum extent permitted under Section 409A. If this recalculation reveals an overpayment, the Plan Administrator must take appropriate steps to recover it. It is specifically intended that there be no duplication of payments under this Plan or any specified plans to the maximum extent allowed under Section 409A. Effective January 1, 2009, if a Participant has earned a benefit under a plan maintained by a member of the PepsiCo Organization that is a “qualifying plan” under the “Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.8 of Part A of the Salaried Plan or the “Transfers and Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.5 of Part B of the Salaried Plan, those rules apply when calculating the Participant’s Total Pension under Section 5.1(c)(1) only to the extent that applying them would not result in a change in the time or form of payment of the 409A pension that is prohibited by Section 409A. For the purpose of this limit on offsets, the Company intends to make special arrangements with respect to the payment of the benefit under the qualifying plan that are legally permissible under that plan and compliant with Section 409A, to avoid any such change in time or form of payment to the maximum extent possible; if such Section 409A-compliant arrangements are timely implemented in a particular situation, the limit on offsets in the prior sentence does not apply. An executive who has signed a written agreement with the Company waiving eligibility under the Plan (even if otherwise meeting the Employee definition) or agreeing not to participate in the Plan shall not thereafter be entitled to a benefit or any increase in benefits related to such employment (whichever applies). Such written agreements may be entered into before or after eligibility or participation begins and may take any form deemed effective by the Company. This Section 5.5 applies to agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2009. A Participant’s Pre-409A Pension is the portion of their Pension grandfathered under Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv), and principles similar to those in Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) apply in determining it. The Company may reduce any payment or benefit payable to or on behalf of a Participant by the amount of any obligation the Participant owes to the Company that is or becomes due and payable, provided (1) the obligation was incurred during the employment relationship, (2) the reduction during any Plan Year does not exceed the amount allowed under Code Section 409A, and (3) the reduction is made at the same time and in the same amount as the obligation otherwise would be due and collectable. Additionally, if a Participant has earned a 409A Benefit (a “Prior 409A Benefit”) that was paid before or will become payable under different payment terms than an additional 409A Benefit, the calculation of the additional 409A Benefit shall include an offset for the Prior 409A Benefit. This offset is determined as of the Annuity Starting Date of the additional 409A Benefit on a basis that (i) accounts for applicable reductions for early or late commencement as of that date, (ii) reflects, if applicable and customary, the relative value of forms of payment, and (iii) otherwise adjusts the offset to its Actuarial Equivalent in each respect as appropriate and customary under the circumstances and in accordance with rules authorized by the Plan Administrator. For example, when a Participant is entitled to Post-Disability Accruals after having earned Pre-Separation Accruals, an offset of the Pre-Separation Accruals will apply in determining the Post-Disability Accruals. The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner under Section 4.12 is determined as follows: (1) the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension, reduced by (2) the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension, and then further reduced by (but not below zero) (3) the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program. This amount is determined on a basis that (i) takes into account applicable reductions for early or late commencement, and (ii) adjusts the reductions in (a)(2) and (3) to their Actuarial Equivalent as appropriate under the circumstances and pursuant to rules of the Plan Administrator, including to account for the time and form of any prior payments. Definitions include: (1) “Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension” means the greater of (i) the amount of the Eligible Domestic Partner’s pre-retirement domestic partner’s pension under the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code as interpreted and applied under the Salaried Plan or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan, or (ii) the amount (if any) of the Eligible Domestic Partner’s PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension under subsection (c), calculated as if payable as of what would be the Normal Retirement Date of the Participant related to the Eligible Domestic Partner. The greater benefit is then reduced or increased for commencement before or after such Normal Retirement Date. (2) “Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension” means the amount of the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension under the Salaried Plan. (3) “Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program” means the amount of the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension under the Pre-409A Program. The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension is determined under paragraph (1) or (2) below, whichever applies, with reference to the PEP Guarantee (if any) that would have been available to the Participant under Section 5.2. (1) Normal Rule: The Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension payable under this paragraph shall equal the amount that would be payable as a survivor annuity under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant had (i) separated from service on the date of death (or earlier, actual Separation from Service), (ii) commenced a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity on the same date payments of the Qualified Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension are to commence, and (iii) died on the day immediately following such commencement. (2) Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension paid on behalf of a Participant described in Section 4.6(a) shall not be less than 25 percent of such Participant’s PEP Guarantee determined under Section 5.2. For this purpose, Credited Service is determined as provided in Section 3.3(c)(2) of the Salaried Plan, and the deceased Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation are determined as of his date of death. A Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension under this paragraph is not reduced for early commencement. Principles similar to those in (i) Section 5.1(b) and (ii) the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) apply in determining the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension under this section. Article VI governs the distribution of benefits to a Participant entitled to a 409A Pension and the continuation of benefits to such Participant’s beneficiary upon death. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension derived from the 409A Program shall be payable as an Annuity for the life of the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, as applicable, subject to Section 4.9 (cashout distributions). The distribution of a Pre-409A Pension is governed by the terms of the Pre-409A Program. 6.1 Form and Timing of Distributions: (a) 409A Retirement Pension: A Participant’s 409A Retirement Pension shall generally be distributed as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Participant’s Retirement Date, subject to paragraph (2) and Section 6.6 (delay for Key Employees). (2) Prior Payment Election: A Participant entitled to a 409A Retirement Pension who made an election (i) up to and including December 31, 2007, and (ii) at least six months prior to and in a calendar year prior to the Participant’s Annuity Starting Date may receive the benefit in accordance with such election. The election allows a Participant to choose either (i) to receive the benefit in an Annuity form, (ii) to commence distribution at a time other than as provided in paragraph 6.1(a)(1), or both (i) and (ii). A payment election made by a Participant only eligible to receive a Vested Pension on Separation from Service is disregarded. Subject to Section 4.9 (cashouts), a Participant who validly elects to receive an Annuity shall receive the benefit as a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married or as a Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless they elect one of the optional forms of payment described in Section 6.2 in accordance with the election procedures in Section 6.3(a). A Participant is considered married if married on their Annuity Starting Date (with such date determined taking into account any applicable election). If a Participant’s benefit commences later than under paragraph 6.1(a)(1) due to an election under this paragraph, the benefit will be increased for earnings at the interest rate used to compute the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value through the date the check is prepared, which interest is paid at the time elected by the Participant under this paragraph. (b) 409A Vested Pension: Subject to Section 4.9, Section 6.6, and subsection (c) below, a Participant’s 409A Vested Pension shall be distributed in accordance with paragraph (1) or (2) below, unless, in the case of a Participant who is married (as determined under the standards in paragraph 6.1(a)(2)) or has an Eligible Domestic Partner on their Annuity Starting Date, they elect one of the optional forms of payment distributions in Section 6.2 in accordance with the election procedures in Section 6.3(a): (1) Separation Prior to Age 55: For a Participant who separates from service with at least five years of service prior to age 55, the 409A Vested Pension shall be distributed as an Annuity commencing on the first of the month coincident with or immediately following the date they attain age 55, which shall be the Annuity Starting Date of their 409A Vested Pension. The distribution shall be a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married or a Single Life Annuity if not married; provided that an unmarried Participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% Survivor Annuity or 75% Survivor Annuity with their Eligible Domestic Partner as beneficiary as provided in Section 6.2. A Participant is considered married or to have an Eligible Domestic Partner for purposes of this paragraph if married or has an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date of their 409A Vested Pension. (2) Separation at Ages 55 Through 64: For a Participant who separates from service with at least five years but less than ten years of service and on or after age 55 but prior to age 65, the 409A Vested Pension shall be distributed as an Annuity (as provided in paragraph (1)) commencing on the first of the month following their Separation from Service. (c) Disability Pension: The portion of a Participant’s 409A Disability Pension representing Pre-Separation Accruals shall be paid on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s attainment of age 55 and (ii) the Participant’s Separation from Service. The available forms of payment for the portion representing Pre-Separation Accruals shall be those available to a Participant entitled to a Vested Pension or a Retirement Pension, as set forth in Section 6.2 (including, to the extent applicable, different forms available to a married Participant or Participant with a domestic partner versus a single Participant). The portion representing Post-LTD Accruals shall be paid on the first day of the month following the Participant’s attainment of age 65 in a lump sum. 6.2 Available Forms of Payment: This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant entitled to a Retirement Pension under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) or a Vested Pension under subsection 6.1(b). (a) Basic Forms: A Participant entitled to a Retirement Pension may choose one of the following optional forms of payment by making a valid election in accordance with the election procedures in Section 6.3(a). A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension and married on their Annuity Starting Date may choose one of the optional forms available under paragraph (1), (2)(ii), or (2)(iii) below with their Eligible Spouse as beneficiary (and no other optional form under this subsection shall be permitted to such a Participant). A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension, not married, and with an Eligible Domestic Partner on their Annuity Starting Date may choose one of the optional forms available under paragraph (2)(ii) or (2)(iii) below with their Eligible Domestic Partner.

This section outlines the payment options available to a Participant entitled to a Retirement Pension under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) or a Vested Pension under subsection 6.1(b). A Participant entitled to a Retirement Pension may choose one of the optional forms of payment by making a valid election in accordance with the procedures in Section 6.3(a). A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension who is married on their Annuity Starting Date may select one of the optional forms under paragraphs (1), (2)(ii), or (2)(iii) with their Eligible Spouse as beneficiary, and no other optional form is permitted. A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension who is not married and has an Eligible Domestic Partner on their Annuity Starting Date may choose one of the forms under (2)(ii) or (2)(iii) with their Eligible Domestic Partner as beneficiary, and no other optional form is permitted. A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension who is not married and has no Eligible Domestic Partner on their Annuity Starting Date shall receive a Single Life Annuity. Each optional annuity is actuarially equivalent to the Single Life Annuity. The Single Life Annuity Option provides monthly payments ending with the last payment due prior to the Participant’s death. The Survivor Options include: (i) 100 Percent Survivor Option, where the Participant receives a reduced 409A Pension for life, and payments continue at the same reduced amount to the beneficiary for life, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’s death and ending with the last payment due prior to the beneficiary’s death; (ii) 75 Percent Survivor Option, where payments of 75 percent of the reduced amount continue to the beneficiary under the same conditions; (iii) 50 Percent Survivor Option, where payments of 50 percent of the reduced amount continue to the beneficiary under the same conditions, and a 50 percent survivor option is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse; and (iv) Ten Years Certain and Life Option, where the Participant receives a reduced 409A Pension for at least 120 months, and if the Participant dies before 120 payments, the remaining payments are made to the primary beneficiary (or contingent beneficiary if the primary has predeceased the Participant). Inflation protection may be provided at 5 percent or 7 percent levels, where the monthly benefit is initially reduced but increased if inflation in the prior year exceeds the selected threshold, with the increase being the difference between inflation and the threshold. Inflation is measured based on the 12-month period ending September 30, using the same method as for Social Security cost-of-living adjustments, and the protection applies to survivor benefits. Inflation protection elections are irrevocable by the Participant or their surviving beneficiary. Elections must be in writing, signed by the Participant, and received by the Plan Administrator at least one day prior to the Annuity Starting Date, specifying the form of payment and beneficiary if applicable. Electronic media elections are acceptable if permitted by the Plan Administrator. For Participants with multiple Annuity Starting Dates, elections apply to all unpaid accruals as of the initial Annuity Starting Date, except that for a rehired Participant who was previously receiving an Annuity or had a lump sum distribution (other than a cashout), the subsequent Annuity Starting Date applies only to benefits accruing after rehire, and prior accruals continue under the initial election. Effective January 1, 2014, the Plan Administrator assumes a Participant is unmarried on their Annuity Starting Date unless the Participant provides notice to the Plan prior to that date, deemed sufficient by the Administrator, that they are married. Spousal consent is not required for a valid election. Special rules for survivor options state that if a Participant or their beneficiary dies before the Annuity Starting Date, the election is disregarded; if the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date but before pension commencement, payments begin to the surviving spouse, domestic partner, or other beneficiary on the first day of the month following death, with any back payments going to the estate. For the Ten Years Certain and Life Option, if the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date, without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before 120 payments, the remaining payments go to the estate; if a beneficiary dies before payments are completed, the remaining payments go to the beneficiary’s estate. If the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, the Participant may not elect the 100 percent survivor option if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger, or the 75 percent survivor option if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger. A Participant who elects a survivor option must designate a beneficiary on the election form or an approved form, with the ability to name both a primary and contingent beneficiary under the Ten Years Certain and Life Option. A Participant may change or revoke their beneficiary designation at any time prior to the Annuity Starting Date, in accordance with Plan Administrator rules, and the designation is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator. If no beneficiary is designated and a survivor option is elected, the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, as applicable. A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if an optional form of payment is permitted, the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date. For Key Employees, distributions commence on the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation from Service (or earlier if death occurs), except for periods before 2009 when no delay applies if the 409A Pension commences at the same time as the Salaried Plan pension. For Vested Pensions, distributions commence as per Section 6.1(b), or if later, on the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation from Service (or earlier if death occurs), with the same exception for pre-2009 periods. Any delayed payments are increased by interest at the rate used to compute the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value through the date of payment, and are paid as a lump sum on the applicable payment date. If a beneficiary or estate receives payments due to death, the delayed payments are made with the same interest. A portion of the 409A Pension is paid as a lump sum to the IRS to satisfy the Participant’s FICA Amount and related income tax withholding at source, as required by Code Section 3401 or applicable state, local, or foreign tax laws. The lump sum is paid on the date the FICA Amount and related tax are due, and the Participant’s 409A Pension is reduced by the actuarial equivalent of this lump sum, effective on the payment date, even if that date is after the start of the pension. This reduction does not affect the commencement date of the pension, including any required delay for Key Employees. The Plan is administered by the Plan Administrator.

The lump sum payment used to satisfy a Participant’s FICA Amount and related income tax withholding will be reduced, effective as of the date of payment of the lump sum, to the actuarial equivalent of that lump sum, and this reduction may occur even after the date the Participant’s 409A Pension commences. The Participant’s 409A Pension will commence in accordance with the Plan’s terms and the lump sum payment will not affect the timing of the 409A Pension payment, including any required delay for a Key Employee. The Plan is administered by the Plan Administrator, who has the authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, perform benefit calculations, and rely on information provided by the Participant, such as mailing address, age, and marital status. The Plan Administrator’s interpretations, determinations, regulations, and calculations are final and binding. Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is considered a fiduciary, and restrictions under section 406 of ERISA do not apply. If a person entitled to a benefit is under a legal disability or incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may make payments to the person or their legal representative or apply the payment for the person’s benefit, and such payments will fully discharge any liability under the Plan. The Plan Administrator has exclusive discretion to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility, and set benefit amounts, and this discretion is absolute—even if not expressly granted or required by the Plan—and may consider the Company’s intent. All decisions are final, conclusive, and binding. The Plan Administrator may modify the claims review process as long as it includes the required steps. A claim must be submitted in writing or in an acceptable form. Within 90 days of receiving the claim, the Plan Administrator must notify the claimant of: (a) the specific reason(s) for denial, (b) the relevant Plan provisions, (c) any additional material needed to perfect the claim and why it is necessary, and (d) the claim review procedure, including time limits and the right to bring a civil action under ERISA after a further denial. If special circumstances require an extension, the response period may be extended from 90 to 180 days, with prior notice. The claim review process is available upon written request within 60 days of denial. Upon review, the Plan Administrator will provide a full and fair review, including the opportunity to submit comments, documents, and records, and will consider such submissions regardless of whether they were considered initially. The decision on review will be made within 60 days, or up to an additional 60 days if circumstances warrant, with prior notice. The final decision must be in writing, understandable to the claimant, include specific reasons and references to Plan provisions, and provide the claimant free and reasonable access to all relevant documents, records, and information. Any special extension required by ERISA applies to this Plan in the same way as under the Salaried Plan. Any claim reviewed by a court, arbitrator, or other tribunal will be based solely on the record before the Plan Administrator at the time of the initial determination, and the claimant must first exhaust all claims procedures as described in Section 7.3. The exhaustion requirement applies regardless of the significance of other disputes, to any rights provided by the Plan, whether actual or potential, and even if specific procedures have not been previously defined—where no procedures exist, the Plan Administrator must either promptly establish them or apply the procedures in Section 7.3. The Plan Administrator may make special arrangements to consider claims on a class basis or address unusual conflicts, and such arrangements must be sufficient to ensure exhaustion. For example, exhaustion is not excused for failure to respond to a claim unless the claimant took sufficient steps to make it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that they were submitting a claim, or for failure to fulfill a document request unless (A) the claimant is lawfully entitled to the documents, (B) the request is in writing and received by the Plan Administrator, (C) the documents are not provided within six months or a reasonable longer period, and (D) the claimant made it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that they were entitled to the documents and that the documents are material to a colorable claim. For purposes of this Section, a “Dispute” includes any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or other matter, and a “Claim” includes any Dispute that relates to the interpretation of the Plan, its terms or conditions, applicable law, validity of the Plan, administration, compliance with ERISA or other law, requests for benefits, assertions of fiduciary breaches, or any matter the Plan Administrator deems similar or related to the Plan. A “Claimant” includes any actual or putative Employee, former Employee, Participant, former Participant, beneficiary, spouse, former spouse, domestic partner, estate, heir, representative, or any group of such individuals or entities who have a Claim. The Plan is intended to be administered in good faith and in accordance with ERISA, and as a condition for any right or recovery, the Plan imposes a contractual obligation for complete exhaustion of claims procedures to ensure efficient and uniform resolution and to protect the Plan from substantial litigation costs. Any claim or action alleging wrongful denial of benefits or interference with ERISA-protected rights must be filed within two years of the date the cause of action accrues. A cause of action for benefits accrues not later than the earliest of (i) when the benefit calculation is received, (ii) the date payments are identified to commence, (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the basis of the claim, or (iv) when the benefit is first paid or denied. A cause of action for alleged interference with ERISA-protected rights accrues when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interference. For any other claim, the cause of action accrues within two years of the claimant’s actual or constructive knowledge of the facts giving rise to the claim. Failure to file within this two-year period will preclude the claim. Communications pursuant to the mandatory appeals process do not extend the two-year period. Any claim or action related to the Plan filed in court or by a Petitioner must be brought only in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, effective for claims filed on or after January 1, 2011. Nothing in the Plan constitutes a contract of employment, a right to continued employment, or a limitation on an employer’s right to discharge employees. Benefits under the Plan and the right to future benefits are not subject to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer, assignment, pledge, encumbrance, charge, garnishment, execution, or levy, and any such attempt is null and void and not binding on the Company.

Claims or actions filed on or after January 1, 2011, are governed by the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program. Article VIII outlines several key provisions: (8.1) The Plan does not create an employment contract, does not guarantee continued employment, or limit an employer’s right to terminate an employee with or without cause. (8.2) Benefits under the Plan are not subject to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer, assignment, pledge, encumbrance, garnishment, execution, or levy, and any such attempt is null and void; the Company is not liable for the debts, contracts, liabilities, or torts of any person entitled to benefits. (8.3) The Plan is an unfunded plan, and the Company’s obligations are liabilities payable from general funds, with participant rights no greater than those of unsecured general creditors. (8.4) The Company may act under the Plan through the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee, with reports to the Board, or through any person duly authorized by resolution. (8.5) The Company shall indemnify employees acting in good faith within the scope of their employment in administering the Plan to the fullest extent permitted by law. (8.6) The Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A; if it fails to do so, the Company, Board, Plan Administrator, or their designees are not liable for good-faith actions. To avoid benefit duplication, no element such as pensionable earnings or service may be recognized more than once under the Plan or in connection with the Salaried Plan. (8.7) To avoid Section 457A application, a Participant transferring outside the U.S. to provide services to a PepsiCo Organization member that is neither a U.S. corporation nor a pass-through entity wholly owned by a U.S. corporation (a “Covered Transfer”) automatically vests in their Pension as of the last business day before the transfer; benefit accruals for service or age attainment are credited only on the last day of the Plan Year in which such service or age attainment occurs, and only to the extent permitted under subsection (c), and no Benefit Enhancement related to service or age attainment is payable from and after the Covered Transfer if it would constitute compensation includable in income under Section 457A. This exemption does not apply if the Company provides a written communication prior to the transfer stating the subsections do not apply; subsection (b) ceases to apply upon the Participant’s return to service with a U.S. corporation or pass-through entity wholly owned by a U.S. corporation, or as stated in an applicable communication. (8.8) If a Participant transfers to an entity not part of the PepsiCo Organization, the Company retains liability for benefits accrued during employment with PepsiCo, except as otherwise agreed with the new employer. (8.9) Electronic signatures and electronic records have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as manually executed signatures or paper-based records, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law. Article IX governs amendments and termination, with the Company retaining broad rights under applicable law, subject to Section 409A restrictions. The Plan is not contractually guaranteed to continue indefinitely; the Company may amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at its sole discretion, but no amendment or termination shall reduce a Participant’s benefit amount as of the date of such action unless the Participant becomes entitled to an equivalent benefit under another Company plan (except as required to comply with Section 409A); specific forms of payment are not protected. The Company may amend the Plan at its discretion, with or without retroactive effect, including amendments to ensure compliance with Section 409A, and no Employer (other than the Company) may amend the Plan. The Company may terminate the Plan with respect to one or more Employers, a group of Employees experiencing a change in control as defined in Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or as otherwise permitted under Code Section 409A; if terminated for fewer than all Employers, the Plan continues for the remaining Employers. Upon termination, distributions are subject to Section 409A restrictions. In connection with a Change in Control, the Company has maximum discretion to terminate the Plan and make distributions, as permitted under Section 409A, and these terms are exclusive for distributions from the 409A Program. Article X establishes that the Plan, together with the Pre-409A Program documents, comprises three separate ERISA plans effective as of July 1, 1996: (a) an Excess Benefit Plan for Salaried Plan participants exceeding Code section 415 benefits; (b) an Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits in excess of section 401(a)(17) limits (after accounting for Excess Benefit Plan benefits), referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I; (c) a Preservation Top Hat Plan preserving pre-1989 benefit accrual levels for Salaried Plan participants described in section 5.2(a), after accounting for Excess Benefit and Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan benefits, referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II. Benefits are allocated first to the Excess Benefit Plan, then to the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan, then to the Preservation Top Hat Plan, and the plans are severable. Lump sum termination benefits paid under the Plan in connection with a severed employee’s Special Early Retirement (as defined in Appendix Article D) under a temporary severance program are part of the Company’s unfunded severance plan and are considered welfare benefits under ERISA section 3(1), existing only during the temporary severance program and for the purpose of paying severance benefits, and are not subject to top hat plan or pension plan reporting requirements. Article XI states that the Plan is construed and administered under ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and to the extent ERISA does not preempt state law, under the internal laws of New York. If any provision is void, voidable, invalid, or unlawful, the remainder of the Plan remains in effect. Article XII confirms that the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program, as amended and restated, is adopted as of December 19, 2022, and is effective as of January 1, 2022 or as otherwise stated. The document is signed by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer, Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel, and Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel. Appendix Article A provides transition rules effective during the Transition Period from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2008. (A.1) The transition rules apply during that period. (A.2) For Article II (Definitions), (a) to determine pension amounts in certain annuity forms during the Transition Period, the Salaried Plan’s actuarial factors were used; (b) Key Employee rules include: (1) in 2005, all Participants (and former Participants) classified or grandfathered as Band IV or above for any portion of the 2005 Plan Year were treated as Key Employees for Separation from Service distributions; (2) in 2006 and 2007, individuals who met either (3) were classified or grandfathered as Band IV or above for any portion of the Plan Year prior to their Separation from Service, or (4) would have been a Key Employee as of their Separation from Service date based on compensation (as defined in Code Section 415(c)(3)) were treated as Key Employees.

PepsiCo’s Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program includes specific operating rules for the 2006 and 2007 Plan Years to ensure that all Key Employees are identified for Separation from Service distributions. For those years, the Company treats individuals as Key Employees if they meet either (3) being classified as Band IV or above for any portion of the Plan Year prior to their Separation from Service, or (4) meeting the Key Employee standards as of their Separation from Service date based on compensation as defined in Code Section 415(c)(3). For paragraph (4), compensation used depends on the timing of the Separation from Service: if it occurs in the first calendar quarter of a Plan Year, compensation earned in the calendar year two years prior is used (e.g., for a 2006 first-quarter determination, 2004 compensation is used); if it occurs in the second, third, or fourth quarter, compensation earned in the prior calendar year is used (e.g., for a 2006 second-quarter determination, 2005 compensation is used). Transition rules for distributions state that 409A pensions that would have been paid during the Transition Period under the pre-409A provisions are paid on March 1, 2009. For administration, during the Transition Period, Section 8.6(a) is replaced with language requiring the Plan to operate in compliance with Section 409A and to preserve the grandfathered status of the Pre-409A Program. Any action that violates Section 409A or adversely affects the grandfathered status is void and without effect; if a violation is unavoidable, the rights and effects of the Plan are altered to avoid it. Any provision that violates Section 409A or harms the grandfathered status is void, and any provision required by Section 409A but not expressly stated is deemed to be included. For severance benefits, during the Transition Period, specific provisions apply: for 2005 severance, non-retirement eligible employees receive their 409A pension as a Vested Pension at the same time as their Salaried Plan benefit, or at the later of January 1, 2007 or age 55, with lump-sum payments for retirement-eligible employees who meet retirement requirements as of February 5, 2006, or who receive additional credited service time, or who qualify for Special Early Retirement. For 2007 severance, non-retirement eligible employees receive their 409A pension as a Vested Pension, retirement-eligible employees receive a lump-sum payment on the first day of the month following separation, with exceptions for valid Prior Payment Elections, and employees who become retirement eligible receive their 409A pension on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or separation, with PEP Kicker payments made as a lump sum on the same date. Special retirement eligible employees receive their 409A pension on the first day of the month following age 55, and PEP Kicker payments are made similarly. For 2008 severance, non-retirement eligible employees receive their 409A pension as a Vested Pension, retirement-eligible employees receive a lump-sum payment on the first day of the month following separation, with exceptions for valid Prior Payment Elections, employees who become retirement eligible receive their 409A pension on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or separation, and employees who are or become Special Retirement Eligible receive their 409A pension on the first day of the month following age 55. In all cases, age and years of Elapsed Time Service for Special Early Retirement are rounded up to the nearest whole year when determining eligibility.

Employees who terminate in 2008 as a result of a severance window program and who meet the requirements for Special Early Retirement as of their Separation from Service or during the period between Separation from Service and the end of their paid leave of absence (if any) will have their 409A Pension paid on the first day of the month following their attainment of age 55 as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) of the Plan document, using the forms of payment available to a Participant entitled to a Vested Pension as set forth in Section 6.2 of the Plan document. Any amount paid as a replacement for benefits the Participant could have earned under the Plan due to Separation from Service shall be paid as a single lump sum, provided that if a valid Prior Payment Election was made under Section 6.1(a)(2) of the Plan document, such amounts shall be paid according to that election; all such amounts shall be paid on the first day of the month following the Participant’s attainment of age 55. For Key Employees (as defined in Section A.2(b)) whose 409A Pension is due to Separation from Service, payment is subject to the delay provisions under Section 6.6 of the main Plan document. All payments under this Section A.5 were scheduled to be made during the calendar year of termination, as specified herein, and all Company elections with respect to such payments were made in compliance with Notice 2005-1 and other provisions of Code Section 409A. For Participants who terminate employment in 2005 while classified as Band VI (or equivalent) with a limited duration assignment of less than five years, their PEP Credited Service shall be deemed to be five years, and they shall be deemed vested for purposes of the Plan. A Participant who selects an Annuity Starting Date of November 1, 2007 for their Pension under the Salaried Plan (payable in a single lump sum, after considering Section 6.3(a)(2) if necessary) will have the portion of their benefit not subject to Section 409A paid in a single lump sum six months after their Annuity Starting Date. A Participant who selects a fixed date of payment of February 1, 2005 for their Pension under the Plan will have that date serve as the commencement date of their benefit, and the calculation of their benefit shall include service performed during any period of consulting services provided to the Company, even if after the payment date. For 409A Disability Pension Pre-Separation Accruals, the portion that would have been paid during the Transition Period under the main Plan (excluding permissible transition rules under Section 409A) shall commence on March 1, 2009, with payment forms available as those for a Vested Pension under Section 6.2, including different forms for married versus unmarried Participants. If a Participant who receives Pre-Separation Accruals under A.7(a) dies prior to their expected mortality date (based on the mortality table in Schedule 1 of Section 2.1(b) (Actuarial Equivalent) of the Plan as of January 1, 2009), their beneficiary shall receive the lump sum actuarial equivalent of the annuity payments that would have been made from the date of death until the expected mortality date (had the Participant not died), paid within 30 days of death. A Participant subject to this subsection may name a beneficiary in a form and manner acceptable to the Plan Administrator; if no such beneficiary is named, the beneficiary shall be that selected under Section 6.5 of the Plan, or if none, then the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner (as applicable); if neither exists, the beneficiary shall be the estate. The computation of earnings and service during certain severance windows defines a "Severance Program" as a program providing severance benefits recognized as Service under Section B.3 and Credited Service under Section B.4, and an "Eligible Bonus" as an annual incentive payment identified in the Severance Program as eligible for inclusion in determining the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings. The Plan Administrator may specify that salary continuation and Eligible Bonus received during the first 12 months of a severance leave of absence will be counted toward the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if received after Separation from Service, and if payment of the 409A Pension occurs at Separation from Service and prior to receipt of all such salary or bonus, the Highest Average Monthly Earnings shall be based on the full projected salary and bonus during the first 12 months of the leave, divided between Plan Years to avoid bunching. All Credited Service and Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of a severance period will be counted toward the Participant’s Credited Service and Service for pension calculations, even if occurring after Separation from Service. If a Participant receives additional Credited Service or earnings under Sections B.2 or B.3 as a result of a severance benefit and such additional Credited Service or earnings are included in the pension calculation prior to actual performance or payment, the Pension shall be adjusted actuarially to reflect the early receipt, using the rate under the Salaried Plan for early payment of benefits. This Article C provides special rules for International Transfer Participants and PIRP Transfer Participants. An International Transfer Participant is an individual who, following a transfer to an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary (as defined in paragraph (5) of the Employer definition in Section 2.1 of Part B of the Salaried Plan as in effect on January 1, 2014), would qualify as an Employee (U.S. citizen or resident alien on qualifying temporary international assignment) under paragraph (2)(vi) of the Employee definition in Section 2.1 of Part B of the Salaried Plan as in effect on January 1, 2014, but for being in a position classified as Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher; or, for certain permanent assignments to Mexico, if the assignment is in a Band 4 or higher position, Mexico is the individual’s home country on the records of the Expat Centre for Excellence group or its successor, and the assignment duration is not limited to five years or less. An individual described in subsection (a) or (b) may still qualify if the transfer occurred prior to April 1, 2007, provided the terms of subsection (a) or (b) are satisfied on the date of transfer. The benefit of an International Transfer Participant is calculated by determining a "Total Pension" as if the Participant continued to receive Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan while working for the April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary, without regard to the actual cessation date, except that for transfers prior to 1992, Credited Service and Earnings for employment with the April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary prior to 1992 are not included. The International Transfer Participant’s benefit is then calculated by reducing the Total Pension (expressed as a lump sum on the benefit commencement date) by (1) the amount of the actual benefit under the Salaried Plan (expressed as a lump sum on the benefit commencement date), and (2) any amounts paid from a "qualifying plan" as defined under Section 3.5(c)(4) of Part B of the Salaried Plan with respect to the assignment with the April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary (expressed as a lump sum on the benefit commencement date). The benefit of a PIRP Transfer Participant is determined under Section C.5. Definitions for PIRP Transfer Participants include: "Accrued Benefit" as a single-life annuity payable on the first of the month coincident with or next following the PIRP Transfer Participant’s 65th birthday; "PIRP-DB" as the portion of the PepsiCo International Retirement Program providing defined benefits; "PIRP-DB Employer" as the Company or an affiliate that is an "Employer" under PIRP-DB; "PIRP-DB Pensionable Service" as service qualifying as "Pensionable Service" under PIRP-DB; "PIRP-DB Salary" as compensation qualifying as "Salary" under PIRP-DB; and a "PIRP Transfer Participant" as an individual employed during a year (including a year preceding 2016) by a PIRP-DB Employer in a position eligible to accrue benefits under PIRP-DB (or would be eligible if Section 9 applies). The provisions of this Article relating to International Transfer Participants are effective April 1, 2007, and those relating to PIRP Transfer Participants are effective January 1, 2016 (but may take into account years preceding January 1, 2016). All benefits paid under this Article are subject to Code Section 409A, including any accrued prior to January 1, 2005.

A PIRP Transfer Participant is an individual who either (i) was employed during a year (including a year before 2016) by a PIRP-DB Employer in a position eligible to accrue benefits under PIRP-DB (or would be eligible if Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB did not apply), was then transferred by the Company during that year to a position eligible to accrue benefits under the Salaried Plan, had their PIRP-DB accrual for the Year of Transfer blocked by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB, would otherwise be entitled to a PIRP-DB benefit enhancement for the Year of Transfer related to PIRP-DB Salary or PIRP-DB Pensionable Service, and whose PIRP-DB benefit was not already paid out by December 1, 2016 (with any such paid-out benefit that the PIRP-DB Vice President determines should be treated as if not paid out being disregarded), or (ii) was employed during a year (including a year before 2016) by an Employer in a position eligible to accrue benefits under the Salaried Plan, was then transferred by the Company during that year to a position eligible to accrue benefits under PIRP-DB (or would be eligible if Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB did not apply), had their PIRP-DB accrual for the Year of Transfer blocked by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB, would otherwise be entitled to a PIRP-DB benefit enhancement for the Year of Transfer related to PIRP-DB Salary or PIRP-DB Pensionable Service, and whose PIRP-DB benefit was not already paid out by December 1, 2016 (with any such paid-out benefit that the PIRP-DB Vice President determines should be treated as if not paid out being disregarded). The “PIRP-DB Vice President” is the Company executive who holds the role of “Vice President” under the terms of PIRP-DB. A “U.S. Person” is an individual classified as such under the terms of PIRP-DB. The “Year of Transfer” is the year in which a transfer described in subsection (f) occurs. A PIRP Transfer Participant’s benefit under the Plan is determined using a methodology substantially similar to that in Section 5.1 of the Plan, with their “Total Pension” calculated as if they were an eligible employee under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer and as if they received Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan equal to their actual Credited Service and Earnings for the Year of Transfer increased by any other compensation and service that would have been recognized as PIRP-DB Salary and PIRP-DB Pensionable Service if Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB did not apply. If a PIRP Transfer Participant would be credited with PIRP-DB Salary that cannot be recognized under PIRP due to Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB and this PIRP-DB Salary would be considered for accrual purposes under PIRP-DB in connection with PIRP-DB Pensionable Service not recognized under this Plan, the increase in the PIRP Transfer Participant’s Accrued Benefit under PIRP related to this PIRP-DB Pensionable Service and blocked by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB shall be added to their Accrued Benefit under this Plan. For a PIRP Transfer Participant with a Separation from Service on or after January 1, 2017, this increase shall result in an appropriate increase, determined in the Company’s discretion, in the Total Pension determined under paragraph (1). In determining Credited Service and Earnings, no compensation or service shall be taken into account more than once, and the Total Pension shall be determined to avoid duplication of benefits that will be provided to or on behalf of the PIRP Transfer Participant under PIRP-DB (after applying Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB) or another plan maintained or contributed to by the Company or an affiliate, without applying any offset that would violate Code Section 409A. The PIRP Transfer Participant’s benefit shall be calculated by reducing their Total Pension as determined under subsection (a) by the reductions normally applicable under Article V.
