Effective May 1, 2009, this Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of a transferred Participant whose transfer would be an Eligible Transfer under Section TRI.2(e) of the Part B of the Salaried Plan but for the fact that such individual is reemployed by the Company on or after May 1, 2009 into a position classified as Band 4 or higher. For purposes of determining such Participant’s Total Pension within the meaning of Section 5.1(c)(1), but not for purposes of determining their Salaried Plan Pension within the meaning of Section 5.1(c)(2), such Participant’s position on reemployment will be deemed to be classified as below Band 4 (or its equivalent), so that the Participant’s transfer is eligible to be treated as an Eligible Transfer (subject to other conditions) and the Participant is eligible for the imputed service provisions of Section TRI.4(b) and (c). Such Participant’s benefit otherwise shall be subject to the Plan’s usual conditions and shall be paid in accordance with the Plan’s usual terms. All benefits paid under this Article are subject to Code section 409A. This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below). This Article is effective for Participants who are terminated in a Severance Program or under circumstances that qualify them for an Individual Severance Agreement (each as defined in Section E.2 below) on or after January 1, 2009 (or in the case of Participants covered by Appendix Article PBG, on or after January 1, 2012). Nothing in this Article E shall make any of the additional benefits made available under the Plan in any Severance Program or pursuant to any Individual Severance Agreement a permanent feature of the Plan. A “Covered Participant” means a Participant whose employment with the Company is terminated and who is eligible for Special Early Retirement either (i) under a Severance Program and pursuant to the terms of the Applicable Summary Plan Description, or (ii) pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement. An “Individual Severance Agreement” means an agreement between the Company and a Covered Participant that (i) sets forth the terms and conditions of the Covered Participant’s termination of employment and (ii) expressly either (A) provides that the termination qualifies the Covered Participant for Special Early Retirement under PEP, or (B) describes the pension benefits the Covered Participant will receive in connection with the termination of employment. A “Kicker” means the Special Early Retirement benefit provided to a Covered Participant pursuant to the terms of an Applicable Summary Plan Description or an Individual Severance Agreement and that is equal to (i) the Participant’s benefit under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of his Termination Date, determined based on the benefit formulas and early retirement reduction factors for Early Retirement Pensions under each plan, minus (ii) the Participant’s Vested Pension under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of the Termination Date, determined based on the benefit formulas and reduction factors for Vested Pensions under each plan. The Kicker shall be divided into the following components: (1) the “PEP Kicker,” which is the portion of the Kicker paid under the Plan as a replacement for benefits the Participant could have earned under the Plan but for their Separation from Service (either in a Severance Program or pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement) prior to attaining Normal or Early Retirement under the Plan; and (2) the “Qualified Kicker,” which is the portion of the Kicker paid under the Plan as a replacement for benefits the Participant could have earned under the Salaried Plan but for their termination of employment (either in a Severance Program or pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement) prior to attaining Normal or Early Retirement under the Salaried Plan. In determining the early retirement reduction factors for ages before 55, the monthly rate of reduction applicable between age 56 and age 55 shall apply unless (i) in the case of a Participant who is eligible for Special Early Retirement under a Severance Program, a different factor is used in the Salaried Plan for employees covered by the same Severance Program in which case such other factor shall be used, and (ii) in the case of a Participant who is eligible for Special Early Retirement pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement, a different factor is called for therein, in which case such other factor shall be used. “Severance Program” has the same meaning as under Appendix Section ERW.2(f) of Part B of the Salaried Plan (legacy PepsiCo Appendix). “Special Early Retirement” means a retirement from the Company that either (i) satisfies all conditions for receiving special early retirement benefits set forth in an Applicable Summary Plan Description, or (ii) is expressly recognized as qualifying for special early retirement benefits pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement. “Termination Date” means the later of (i) the Covered Participant’s Separation from Service, or (ii) the date as of which the Covered Participant’s authorized severance leave of absence (if any) is projected to terminate under the terms of the Applicable Summary Plan Description or the Individual Severance Agreement, as applicable. If clause (ii) of the preceding sentence applies, then a Participant’s Termination Date shall be determined as of the date of the Participant’s Separation from Service using the formulas for calculating the severance leave of absence, as such formulas are in effect under the Applicable Summary Plan Description or the Individual Severance Agreement when the legally binding right to special early retirement benefits arises in connection with the Severance Program or pursuant to the Individual Severance Agreement (or if special early retirement benefits do not apply to the Covered Participant, as of the date determined by the Plan Administrator). Except as otherwise expressly provided in the Applicable Summary Plan Description or the Individual Severance Agreement, a Participant’s Termination Date, once set in accordance with the prior two sentences, shall not change based on any circumstances or events that follow the date of the Participant’s Separation from Service. A Covered Participant’s 409A Pension (calculated without regard to the Kicker for purposes of this Section E.3) shall be paid as follows: (a) Non-Retirement Eligible Participants: If a Covered Participant is not eligible for Retirement as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’s 409A Pension shall be paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to Vested Pensions under Section 6.2. (b) Retirement Eligible Participants: (1) If the Covered Participant is eligible for a Normal, Early or Late Retirement Pension under Article IV as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’s 409A Pension shall be paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1); provided, however, that if the Participant made a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2), his 409A Pension shall be paid as a Retirement Pension in accordance with such election. (2) If the Covered Participant becomes eligible for a Normal or Early Retirement Pension after his Separation from Service, including during the period between his Separation from Service and the last day of his paid leave of absence (if any), the Participant’s 409A Pension shall be paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to Vested Pensions under Section 6.2. (c) Special Early Retirement Eligible Participants: If a Covered Participant is eligible for Special Early Retirement as of his Separation from Service or becomes so eligible during the period between his Separation from Service and the last day of his paid leave of absence (if any), the Participant’s 409A Pension shall be paid in accordance with the applicable provisions for Special Early Retirement.

Under Article IV, a Participant’s 409A Pension is paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), provided that if the Participant made a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2), the 409A Pension is paid as a Retirement Pension in accordance with that election. If a Covered Participant becomes eligible for a Normal or Early Retirement Pension after Separation from Service, including during the period between Separation from Service and the last day of any paid leave of absence, the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to Vested Pensions under Section 6.2. For Special Early Retirement Eligible Participants, if such eligibility exists as of Separation from Service or during the period between Separation from Service and the last day of any paid leave of absence, the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to Vested Pensions under Section 6.2. A Covered Participant’s PEP Kicker is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s 55th birthday or (ii) Separation from Service, except that if a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) was made, the PEP Kicker is paid according to that election, even if the 409A Pension is paid under Section E.3(b)(2). If the Participant dies after meeting the requirements for a PEP Kicker but before payment, the PEP Kicker is paid to the Surviving Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner in a single lump sum 60 days after death, or to the Participant’s estate if no such spouse or partner exists. A Qualified Kicker is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month coincident or next following the Termination Date, unless the Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement expressly provides for a different time or form of payment, in which case those provisions govern. If the Participant dies after meeting the requirements for a Qualified Kicker but before payment, the Qualified Kicker is paid to the Surviving Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner in a single lump sum 60 days after death, or to the Participant’s estate if no such spouse or partner exists. If a Participant is determined to be a Key Employee, any payment under Article E due to Separation from Service is subject to the required delay under Section 6.6, except to the extent the payment qualifies for an exemption under Section 409A. Article F applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F.2, who must (i) become subject to U.S. income taxes (Engage in U.S. Service), (ii) continue to accrue benefits under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after Engaging in U.S. Service, (iii) have accrued benefits under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for such period, (iv) either be localized in the U.S. as a PepsiCo employee or terminate employment before commencing a U.S.-outside assignment, and (v) be designated by the Company in its unfettered discretion as a Covered U.K. Employee. The period of U.S. Service begins on the first day of U.S. tax subjectivity (U.S. Commencement Date) and ends on the date the individual is no longer subject to U.S. income taxes or, if earlier, the date Plan benefits under Article F commence (U.S. Cessation Date). A Covered U.K. Employee’s benefit is determined by calculating, as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date, the “Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit” minus the “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit.” The Modified U.S. Cessation Date is the earliest of (i) the date no longer subject to U.S. income taxes, (ii) the date the first clause of Section F.2(iv) is satisfied, (iii) the date commencing an assignment outside the U.S., or (iv) the date benefits under Article F commence. The Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit is the total benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix based on all service and compensation through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date, expressed as a single lump sum payable upon the commencement of benefits under Article F. The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is the total benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix as of immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, also expressed as a single lump sum payable upon the commencement of benefits under Article F. The calculation follows the operating rules in Section F.4. Accruals after the U.S. Cessation Date do not reduce the benefit under Article F, except that if such accruals exceed the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix accruals, the excess (as a lump sum) is offset against the benefit under Article F to the extent it does not violate Code Section 409A. The actuarial assumptions used in determining the lump sum value comply with Code Section 417(e) and are the assumptions that would be used under the Salaried Plan to pay a retirement lump sum as of the applicable date. The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is determined as if the employee voluntarily terminated employment immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date. If the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan or U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix is amended during a year in a way that would change the Section F.3 calculation and applies earlier than the following year, the amendment is delayed to be prospectively effective starting the following year, to the extent necessary to comply with Code Section 409A. If a Covered U.K. Employee has earned a benefit under Article F, reaches the U.S. Cessation Date, and then again Engages in U.S. Service and meets all requirements to be a Covered U.K. Employee, the terms are reapplied to determine if a benefit is earned for the new period, except that any resulting benefit is reduced by the lump sum value of any prior benefit to avoid duplication. If a Covered U.K. Employee has earned a benefit under Article F, reaches the U.S. Cessation Date, and then is employed in a classification eligible for accruals under other Plan provisions, those provisions are applied to determine if a benefit is earned for the new period, except that any resulting benefit is reduced by the lump sum value of any prior benefit to avoid duplication. A Covered U.K. Employee is not entitled to any other benefits under the Plan or the Salaried Plan while a Covered U.K. Employee, and prior to satisfying all requirements, has no legally binding right to a benefit under Article F. The Company may take action at any time before full eligibility to prevent an individual from becoming entitled to a benefit under Article F, in its unfettered discretion. Article G provides a one-time opportunity for Participants who Separated from Service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension with a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date to make a Delay Election under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C). This Article is effective as of January 1, 2018. To be eligible, a Participant must have Separated from Service before January 1, 2018, be eligible for a 409A Vested Pension with a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date, and be selected and notified by the Company in its sole discretion. A Delay Election must become fully effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the previous Scheduled Payment Date and specify a new scheduled date for payment commencement that is at least 5 years later than the Scheduled Payment Date but not later than the first of the month coincident with or immediately following the Participant’s 65th birthday. A Delay Election does not permit a change in form of payment except that the form of annuity is determined by the Participant’s marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date (determined under Section 6.3(c)) and any reduction for early commencement is determined with reference to the New Scheduled Payment Date. Article H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for periods prior to January 1, 2019. Appendix Article I provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program for certain Pre-409A Participants to avoid a material modification of the Pre-409A Program by adjusting early commencement reductions of Vested Pensions payable as annuities to use the 2019 Salaried Program Factors. The PepsiCo Salaried Employees Retirement Plan, as amended from time to time, governs the Salaried Plan, and a Participant’s benefit under this Plan is determined solely by reference to Part C of the Salaried Plan. A Salaried Plan Participant is an Employee who participates in the Salaried Plan. Section 409A of the Code and applicable regulations and guidance issued thereunder apply. Benefits not payable under the Salaried Plan due to Section 415 limitations are excluded. Separation from Service is defined under Section 409A. A Single Lump Sum is the distribution of a Participant’s total PEP Pension in excess of their Grandfathered Benefit in a single payment. A Specified Employee is any Participant who, during an applicable year, is: (i) an officer of any member of the PBG Organization with annual compensation greater than $130,000 (adjusted under Section 416(i)(1) of the Code); (ii) a 5-percent owner of any member of the PBG Organization; or (iii) a 1-percent owner of any member of the PBG Organization with annual compensation over $150,000. For (i), no more than 50 employees with the highest annual compensation are treated as officers. Annual compensation means compensation as defined in Treas. Reg. § 1.415(c)-2(a), without regard to Treas. Reg. §§ 1.415(c)-2(d), 1.415(c)-2(e), and 1.415(c)-2(g). The Plan Administrator determines Specified Employees in accordance with Section 416(i) of the Code and applicable regulations or guidance, with the applicable year determined under Section 409A and any modifications under Section 409A applied. Except as required by Section 409A, Specified Employees are determined as of the last day of each calendar year based on compensation for that year, and such designation is effective for a twelve-month period beginning on April 1 of the following calendar year. Additionally, all Employees classified as E5 and above on the applicable determination date (last day of each calendar year) are treated as Specified Employees for the twelve-month period beginning on April 1, unless there are at least 200 Specified Employees without regard to this provision; if fewer than 200, but full application would exceed 200, then those E5 and above employees with the lowest base salaries are excluded. Between February 26, 2010, and March 31, 2010, Specified Employees are identified by combining the pre-transaction separate lists of Specified Employees from all Employers, to comply with Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(i)(6)(i). On and after April 1, 2010, Key Employees are identified as follows: (i) from April 1, 2010, to March 31, 2011, an employee is a Specified Employee (subject to subparagraph (iii)) if classified as at least Band IV or its equivalent on December 31, 2009, defined as a Band IV employee or above in a PepsiCo Business, a Level E7 or above in a PBG Business, or a Salary Grade 19 or above at a PAS Business; (ii) for the twelve-month period beginning April 1, 2011, and each subsequent April 1, an employee is a Specified Employee (subject to subparagraph (iii)) if they were classified as Band IV or above on the December 31 immediately preceding that April 1. Subparagraph (iii) states that an employee is a Specified Employee if, as of the preceding December 31, they would be a Specified Employee under Treasury Regulation 1.409A-1(i) or any successor, applying the default rules for the minimum number of specified employees; if combining the rules in (i) or (ii) results in more than 200 individuals, the number is reduced to 200 by eliminating those employees in order of their base compensation from lowest to highest. For purposes of this paragraph, “PAS Business” means each employer, division, or organizational subdivision classified as part of the PAS business; “PBG Business” means each employer, division, or organizational subdivision classified as part of the PBG business; and “PepsiCo Business” means each employer, division, or organizational subdivision classified as part of the PepsiCo business. Article III to Appendix Article PBG - Participation states that each Salaried Plan Participant whose benefit is curtailed by the Compensation Limitation or Section 415 Limitation, or both, and each other Salaried Plan Participant (i) who is a Grandfathered Employee as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan and made elective deferrals to the EID on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011 (inclusive); (ii) who would have been a Grandfathered Participant during April 1, 2009 through December 31, 2010 if not classified as salary band E3-E8 or MP on March 31, 2009; or (iii) whose 1988 pensionable “earnings” under the Salaried Plan, as described in Section 4.2(a), were $75,000 or more, shall participate in this Plan. If the PEP Pension is paid in the same form and commences at the same time as the Salaried Plan pension, the monthly PEP Pension equals the excess of (1) the greater of (i) the monthly pension benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan without regard to (I) the Compensation Limitation; (II) the Section 415 Limitation; (III) the exclusion from Earnings of amounts deferred under the EID on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011; and (IV) the April 1, 2009 through December 31, 2010 exclusion from the Salaried Plan definition of a Grandfathered Participant of a Participant who, as of March 31, 2009, was classified as salary band E3-E8 or MP and had attained age 50 and completed five years of Service or whose sum of age and years of Service was at least 65; and (ii) if applicable, the amount determined in accordance with Section 4.2, expressed in such form and payable as of such time, over (2) the actual monthly pension benefit payable under the Salaried Plan, expressed in such form and payable as of such time. The amount determined, less the Participant’s Grandfathered Benefit, is payable as provided in Section 6.2. If the PEP Pension is paid in a different form or commences at a different time, the PEP Pension is the product of (1) the greater of (i) the monthly pension benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan without regard to (I) the Compensation Limitation; (II) the Section 415 Limitation; (III) the exclusion from Earnings of amounts deferred under the EID on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011; and (IV) the March 31, 2009 through December 31, 2010 exclusion from the Salaried Plan definition of a Grandfathered Participant of a Participant who, as of such date, was classified as salary band E3-E8 or MP and had attained age 50 and completed five years of Service or whose sum of age and years of Service was at least 65; and (ii) if applicable, the amount determined in accordance with Section 4.2, expressed in the form and payable as of such time as applies to the PEP Pension under this Plan, multiplied by (2) a fraction, with numerator equal to the value of the amount determined in Section 4.1(b)(1) reduced by the value of the pension under the Salaried Plan, and denominator equal to the value of the amount determined in Section 4.1(b)(1), with value determined on a reasonable and consistent basis by the Plan Administrator with respect to similarly situated employees. A Participant eligible under subsection (a) of Section 4.2 is entitled to a PEP Guarantee benefit under subsection (b). Eligibility requires 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer of at least $75,000. “1988 pensionable earnings” means the Participant’s remuneration for the 1988 calendar year recognized for benefit accrual under the Salaried Plan as in effect in 1988 and does not include remuneration from an entity during a period when that entity was not an Employer. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined under paragraph (1), subject to special rules in paragraph (2). (1) The amount is determined as follows: (i) three percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus (ii) one percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for each year of Credited Service in excess of 10 years, less (iii) one and two-thirds percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not in excess of 30 years. In determining the amount of a Vested Pension, the PEP Guarantee is first calculated based on (I) the Credited Service the Participant would have earned had they continued to accrue Credited Service until their Normal Retirement Age, and (II) their Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at the earlier of their Severance from Service Date or the date they ceased to accrue additional benefits under both the Salaried Plan and this Plan, and then reduced by multiplying the resulting amount by a fraction, the numerator of which is the Participant’s actual years of Credited Service on the earlier of their Severance from Service Date or the date they ceased to accrue additional benefits under both the Salaried Plan and this Plan, and the denominator of which is the number of years of Credited Service used in the calculation.

The PEP Guarantee is calculated based on (i) the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus (ii) one percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for each year of Credited Service beyond 10 years, less (iii) one and two-thirds percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30 years. To determine the Vested Pension amount, the PEP Guarantee is first calculated using (I) the Credited Service the Participant would have earned had they continued to accrue Credited Service until their Normal Retirement Age, and (II) their Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at the earlier of their Severance from Service Date or the date they ceased to accrue additional benefits under both the Salaried Plan and this Plan, and then reduced by multiplying the resulting amount by a fraction where the numerator is the Participant’s actual years of Credited Service on that earlier date and the denominator is the years of Credited Service they would have earned had they continued to accrue until Normal Retirement Age. Special rules apply: (i) If the Participant has an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner and has commenced receipt of an Annuity, the spouse or partner is entitled to a survivor annuity equal to 50 percent of the Participant’s Annuity, with no reduction in the Participant’s Annuity, and if the surviving spouse or partner is more than 10 years younger, the benefit is reduced by 0.8 percent for each full year between 10 and 20, and by an additional 0.4 percent for each full year over 20; this applies only to participants who retire on or after their Early Retirement Date. (ii) Reductions include: (A) a reduction of 3/12ths of 1 percent per month for each month the benefit commencement date precedes the Normal Retirement Date if an Early Retirement Pension is received; (B) the payment amount is reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of the amount payable at Normal Retirement Date if a Vested Pension is received and payment begins before that date, and any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s coverage reductions apply; (C) if the Participant receives a survivor annuity for a beneficiary who is not an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner, the PEP Guarantee is reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of a Single Life Annuity for the Participant’s life; (D) if the Participant receives an Annuity with inflation protection as described in the Salaried Plan, the PEP Guarantee is reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of the Annuity without such protection. (iii) For a Participant whose Retirement Pension is distributed as a lump sum, the PEP Guarantee amount is the Actuarial Equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, taking into account any survivor benefit under (i) and any early retirement reductions under (ii)(A). (iv) As of April 1, 2009, for a Participant who as of March 31, 2009 was in salary band E3-E8 or MP, attained age 50, completed five years of Service, or had a combined age and years of Service of at least 65, the PEP Guarantee is determined as if they were a Grandfathered Participant on April 1, 2009, so that Earnings and Credited Service were not frozen for April 1, 2009 through December 31, 2010, and Highest Average Monthly Earnings are determined without regard to deferrals under the EID made on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011. For reemployed participants eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after their Annuity Starting Date, non-Grandfathered PEP Pension payments are not suspended, and if additional PEP Pension is accrued after reemployment, the PEP Pension upon subsequent Separation from Service is reduced by the present value of previously distributed PEP benefits as determined by the Plan Administrator. The PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program (the “Plan”) was established in 1972 to allow eligible executives to defer certain cash awards from executive compensation programs. Deferrals earned and vested on or before December 31, 2004 are governed by the Pre-409A Program, while deferrals earned or vested after that date are governed by the 409A Program, as set forth in this document, which became effective as of January 1, 2005 (the “Effective Date”). This document reflects the provisions in effect from and after the Effective Date and governs the rights and benefits of Participants from that date onward, including all distribution trigger events and dates. For actions and events occurring on or after the Effective Date, rights and benefits related to deferrals subject to the 409A Program are governed by this document, while those related to deferrals prior to that date are governed by the Pre-409A Program documents in effect at the time. Together, the 409A Program and Pre-409A Program documents describe the terms of a single plan, but amounts under each program are tracked separately to preserve the Pre-409A Program’s exemption from Section 409A and ensure consistent administration. The 409A Program document was most recently restated effective January 1, 2022, reflecting the sale of the juice business and updating provisions related to exhaustion of administrative remedies. For federal income tax purposes, the Plan is a nonqualified deferred compensation plan that is unfunded and unsecured. Under ERISA, the Plan is intended to be a plan described in Sections 201(2), 301(a)(3), and 401(a)(1) providing unfunded benefits to a select group of management or highly compensated employees. The “Employer” includes PepsiCo, Inc. and any division, subsidiary, or affiliate designated as an Employer by the Plan Administrator, only during the period it is so designated and is a member of the PepsiCo Organization, as listed in Appendix Article A as of January 20, 2022. “ERISA” refers to Public Law 93-406, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended. Reg. §§1.415(c)-2(d), 1.415(c)-2(e), and 1.415(c)-2(g). Effective from and after January 1, 2008, in addition to the foregoing, the Plan Administrator shall treat all other employees classified as LG6 and above (for periods before January 1, 2017, Band IV and above) on the applicable determination date (i.e., the last day of each calendar year) as Key Employees for the twelve-month period beginning on April 1 of the next following calendar year; provided that if this results in more than 200 individuals being counted as Key Employees as of any such determination date, the number will be reduced to 200 by eliminating those employees otherwise added under this subsection in order of their base compensation, from lowest to highest. The net asset value of a phantom unit in one of the phantom funds offered under the Plan is determined as of any date in the same manner as applies to the actual fund that serves as the basis of the phantom fund. A Participant is any Executive qualified to participate in the Plan in accordance with Section 3.01 and who has an Account; an active Participant is one currently deferring under Section 4.01. The PepsiCo Organization refers to the controlled group of organizations of which the Company is a part, as defined by Code Sections 414(b) and (c) and the regulations issued thereunder; an entity is considered a member only during the period it is part of that group. A Performance Period is the 52/53-week fiscal year of the Employer for which Bonus Compensation is calculated and determined, and is deemed to relate to the Plan Year in which the Performance Period ends. The Plan is the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program, as set forth herein and in the Pre-409A Program documents, as it may be amended and restated from time to time (subject to applicable limitations). The Plan Administrator is the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company (Compensation Committee) or its delegate or delegates, who has authority to administer the Plan as provided in Article VII; additionally, the Company’s Senior Vice President, Total Rewards (previously titled Senior Vice President, Compensation and Benefits), or if that position is vacant or eliminated, the person acting to fulfill the majority of its duties (or plurality if no one fulfills a majority) as those duties existed immediately prior to the vacancy or elimination, is delegated operational administration of the Plan, including powers under Section 7.03 and Article VIII. The Senior Vice President may re-delegate operational responsibilities to other persons or parties; accordingly, certain operational responsibilities have been re-delegated to the Recordkeeper. References to the Plan Administrator shall be understood to include the Compensation Committee, the Senior Vice President, and those delegated by the Senior Vice President, except the Recordkeeper. All delegations under this Section are subject to Section 7.06. The Plan Year is a 12-consecutive-month period beginning January 1 and ending December 31. The Pre-409A Program governs deferrals not subject to Section 409A, with its terms set forth in a separate set of documents. Prohibited Misconduct includes: (a) accepting employment, assignment, position, or ownership interest in a business entity that markets, sells, distributes, or produces “Covered Products” (as defined) unless such entity makes retail sales or consumes Covered Products without competing with the PepsiCo Organization; (b) soliciting any PepsiCo Organization employee to leave employment or accept a position with another entity; (c) using or disclosing confidential information about the PepsiCo Organization (including non-public information about customers, suppliers, distributors, business operations, product lines, formulas, pricing, processes, research, financial data, and plans) to a third party, except as necessary in the Participant’s role, with the exception that the Participant may communicate with government agencies, file complaints, participate in investigations, or testify about possible legal violations without notice, and may receive monetary awards for information provided to government agencies, though the Company retains its attorney-client privilege; under the Defend Trade Secrets Act, an individual is not liable for disclosing a trade secret to a government official or attorney solely for reporting or investigating suspected violations of law, or in a sealed complaint or court proceeding, and may use trade secret information in court if the document is filed under seal and the trade secret is not disclosed except pursuant to court order; (d) engaging in acts contrary to the PepsiCo Organization’s best interests, including violating the Company’s Code of Conduct, unlawful trading based on information obtained from employment, or other gross misconduct; (e) engaging in fraudulent activity. “Covered Products” include in-home and commercial beverage systems, carbon dioxide gas cylinders and refills, consumables, ready-to-drink beverages (including carbonated soft drinks, tea, water, juices, juice drinks, sports drinks, coffee drinks, energy drinks), dairy products, snacks (salty, fruit and vegetable, dips, sweet, meat, granola, nutrition and cereal bars, cookies), hot cereals and ready-to-eat cereals, pancake mixes and syrup, grain-based food products, pasta products, sports performance nutrition products (energy, protein, carbohydrate, nutrition, meal replacement chews, bars, powders, gels, drinks or drink mixes), or any product or service the Participant had reason to know was under development during employment. “Participation” includes serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor; providing input, advice, guidance, or suggestions; or providing a recommendation or testimonial on behalf of such a business entity or its products. The Recordkeeper is the party delegated, under the authority of the Plan Administrator, to maintain Participant Account records, process transactions, and perform other duties as established by the Plan Administrator. Retirement occurs when a Participant separates from service after attaining (whichever occurs earlier): (a) age 55 with 10 or more years of service, or (b) age 65 with 5 or more years of service. Effective from and after January 1, 2008, a Participant’s “years of service” (for this Section) equals (a) all periods employed by a member of the PepsiCo Organization, plus (b) if employment terminates with all members and the Participant is rehired by a member, the period not employed during rehire; the period prior to first employment with a member is not counted, and the period after termination without rehire is not counted unless rehired (and only upon rehire date). The Second Look Election has the meaning given in Section 4.05. Section 409A refers to Section 409A of the Code and applicable regulations and guidance issued thereunder. Separation from Service is defined in Section 409A; for determining whether a Separation from Service occurs, the Plan uses the twenty percent (20%) test described in Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(h)(3) to identify controlled affiliates of the Company. If a Participant provides services other than as an Executive for the Company and its affiliates (as determined under the prior sentence), such other services are not considered in determining Separation from Service to the extent permitted under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(h)(5) (relating to board members). The term may also be used as a verb (“Separates from Service”) without change in meaning. A Specific Payment Date is a date selected by an Eligible Executive that triggers a lump sum payment or the start of installment payments, as provided in Sections 4.03 and 4.04. The available Specific Payment Dates are determined by the Plan Administrator and are reflected on Election Forms made available by the Plan Administrator. If an Election Form only allows selection of a month or calendar quarter and year, the first day of the selected month or quarter is the Specific Payment Date. An Unforeseeable Emergency is a severe financial hardship due to (a) illness or accident of the Participant, spouse, Beneficiary, or dependent (as defined in Code Section 152(a), without regard to Code Sections 152(b)(1), 152(b)(2), and 152(d)(1)(B)); (b) loss of property due to casualty; or (c) any other similar extraordinary and unforeseeable circumstances beyond the Participant’s control. The Recordkeeper determines the occurrence of an Unforeseeable Emergency in accordance with Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(3) and any guidelines established by the Plan Administrator. U.S. refers to the United States, including its 50 states, the District of Columbia, and its possessions (other than Puerto Rico). A Valuation Date is each business day, as determined by the Recordkeeper, on which Participant Accounts are valued according to current Plan procedures, which may be changed by the Plan Administrator. Article III – Eligibility and Participation: 3.01 Eligibility to Participate: (a) In General. (1) For Plan Years beginning on or after January 1, 2020 and Performance Periods ending after December 31, 2019, subject to Paragraph (3) below and Section 3.05 and the election timing rules of Article IV, an Executive is eligible to defer compensation if, as of the beginning of and throughout the Deferral Window (as described in Section 4.02) related to an upcoming Plan Year and Performance Period, the Executive (i) is classified by the Employer as an Executive in a Leadership Group (“LG”) 2 or above position, (ii) was employed by an Employer during at least a portion of each of the two Plan Years preceding the deferral election, (iii) earned total compensation (including Base Compensation and Bonus Compensation) of more than $200,000 in each such Plan Year (as reflected in the books and records of the Employers), and (iv) has a reasonable expectation of earning more than $200,000 in total compensation (including Base Compensation and Bonus Compensation) in the Plan Year of the deferral election. (2) For Plan Years and Performance Periods preceding those covered by Paragraph (1) and ending after January 1, 2006, subject to Paragraph (3) below and the election timing rules of Article IV, an Executive is eligible to defer compensation 30 days after (i) being hired by an Employer as an Executive classified as LG2 or above (and while remaining so classified) or (ii) being promoted from below LG2 into an LG2 or above position (for periods before January 1, 2017, references to “LG2” shall be applied as references to “Band II”). Any individual who becomes an Eligible Executive during a Plan Year (including one who previously was an Eligible Executive under the Plan or had similar status under another elective account balance plan of a member of the PepsiCo Organization) may only be treated as an Eligible Executive for such Plan Year by satisfying the initial eligibility requirements of Treas. Reg. §1.409A-2(a)(7)(ii). (3) The provisions of this Paragraph (3) shall apply notwithstanding Paragraph (1) or (2) above. From time to time, the Plan Administrator may modify, limit, or expand the class of Executives eligible to defer under the Plan, pursuant to eligibility criteria that need not be uniform among all or any group of Executives; provided that the Plan Administrator may remove an Executive from eligibility only effective as of the end of a Plan Year. An Eligible Executive who makes a valid election that becomes irrevocable (e.g., at the end of a Deferral Window) to participate with respect to Base or Bonus Compensation for a Plan Year or Performance Period (as applicable) shall remain an Eligible Executive for the remainder of the Plan Year or Performance Period and, with respect to Bonus Compensation, until the Eligible Executive’s Bonus Compensation for the Plan Year is deferred, regardless of whether such Executive ceases to meet the eligibility requirements of Paragraph (1) or (2) above, regardless of whether such Executive subsequently is not paid in U.S. dollars or is paid from a non-U.S. payroll, and regardless of whether such Executive is rehired or not.

The provisions of Paragraph (3) apply regardless of Paragraphs (1) or (2) above. The Plan Administrator may, from time to time, modify, limit, or expand the class of Executives eligible to defer under the Plan, using eligibility criteria that do not need to be uniform across all or any group of Executives; however, an Executive may only be removed from eligibility effective at the end of a Plan Year. An Eligible Executive who makes a valid election that becomes irrevocable—such as at the end of a Deferral Window—to participate with respect to Base or Bonus Compensation for a Plan Year or Performance Period (as applicable) shall remain an Eligible Executive for the remainder of that Plan Year or Performance Period, and, with respect to Bonus Compensation, until such Bonus Compensation is deferred, regardless of whether the Executive ceases to meet the eligibility requirements of Paragraphs (1) or (2), whether the Executive subsequently is not paid in U.S. dollars or is paid from a non-U.S. payroll, or whether the individual is transferred to an affiliate of the Company, if such transfer is not a Separation from Service; provided that the occurrence of such events shall cut off any election that has not yet become irrevocable under the Plan Administrator’s rules intended to comply with Section 409A. During the period an individual satisfies all eligibility requirements of this Section, he or she is referred to as an Eligible Executive. Each Eligible Executive becomes an active Participant on the date an amount is first withheld from their compensation pursuant to an Election Form submitted by the Executive to the Recordkeeper (or, if authorized, the Plan Administrator) under Section 4.01. An individual’s eligibility to participate actively by making deferrals (or a deferral election) under Article IV ceases upon the “Election Termination Date” occurring after the earliest of: (a) the date he or she Separates from Service; or (b) the date the Executive ceases to be eligible under criteria described in Section 3.01(a). The “Election Termination Date” is the date as soon as administratively practicable following the date in (a) or (b), or such other date as may be determined by the Plan Administrator’s rules; however, an Election Termination Date does not affect any election already made that has become irrevocable under the Plan’s rules, but it terminates any election that has not yet become irrevocable under the Plan Administrator’s rules intended to comply with Section 409A. An individual who has been an active Participant under the Plan ceases to be a Participant on the date his or her Account is fully paid out; however, participation continues under the Plan if a deferral will be credited to the Participant’s Account in the future (e.g., a deferral of Bonus Compensation paid in a future year). A written agreement between an Employer and a party not part of the PepsiCo Organization regarding the purchase or sale of a business unit, division, or subsidiary (“Business”) may provide for the termination or commencement of participation in the Plan. Absent a specific provision in such agreement to the contrary: (a) each Executive of a Business that is sold shall cease being eligible for the Plan upon such sale (subject to a transitional extension of participation under Section 3.01(a) in the case of a sale that does not result in a Separation from Service as a result of the 20% affiliate rule in the definition of Separation from Service); and (b) no Executive of a Business that is acquired shall be eligible for the Plan except as otherwise designated in the Plan or in such documents related to the Plan as the Plan Administrator may designate from time to time. For purposes of Article IX (amendment and termination of the Plan), an Employer’s approval and execution of a written agreement of acquisition or divesture, as described in the first sentence of this Section, constitutes approval by the Company of the provisions of the agreement relating to participation in this Plan. For Plan Years beginning on or after January 1, 2020 and for Performance Periods ending after December 31, 2019, in the case of an Executive who is an officer within the meaning of Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Section 16 Officer”), the Section 16 Officer’s eligibility shall be determined under the Plan’s provisions in effect as of January 1, 2019 (the “2019 Provisions”) and as provided in this Section 3.05. To comply with the Plan’s exemption under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933 pursuant to Rule 506 of Regulation D, the Plan will comply with Rule 506(b), including by determining the Section 16 Officers’ accredited investor status using any basis permissible under Rule 506(b) (notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 3.01(a)(1)). In addition, in the case of a Section 16 Officer who becomes newly eligible for the Plan under circumstances that qualify for the special 30-day election period permitted by Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-2(a)(7), the Section 16 Officer shall be entitled to make a deferral election for Base Compensation during a 30-day election period pursuant to the 2019 Provisions. Effective on or after January 1, 2010, each Eligible Executive may make an election to defer under the Plan any whole percentage up to 75% of his or her Base Compensation in the manner described in Section 4.02. The Plan Administrator may specify on the Election Form applicable to a particular deferral election (or in other documentation) a lower percentage limitation on the amount of Base Compensation that may be deferred, and any such specification must be made in writing no later than the date the deferral election becomes irrevocable pursuant to Section 4.02. Any changes in such specification from that in effect on January 1, 2019 shall be subject to Section 7.06. Effective on or after May 21, 2010, each Eligible Executive may make an election to defer under the Plan any whole percentage up to 100% of his or her Bonus Compensation in the manner described in Section 4.02. The Plan Administrator may specify on the Election Form applicable to a particular deferral election (or in other documentation) a lower percentage limitation on the amount of Bonus Compensation that may be deferred, and any such specification must be made in writing no later than the date the deferral election becomes irrevocable pursuant to Section 4.02. Any changes in such specification from that in effect on January 1, 2019 shall be subject to Section 7.06. For Performance Periods ending before January 1, 2020, an Eligible Executive who becomes an Eligible Executive during a Plan Year as a result of a promotion from below LG2 into a position that is LG2 or above shall only be eligible to defer Bonus Compensation earned for such Performance Period in which he or she is promoted, if the Eligible Executive (i) is a bonus-eligible Executive for all of such Plan Year and (ii) is promoted by May 15th of the Plan Year in which the promotion occurs (for periods before January 1, 2017, references in this paragraph to “LG2” shall be applied as references to “Band II”). If a promoted Eligible Executive does not satisfy the requirements of the previous sentence, he or she shall not be eligible to defer Bonus Compensation earned for the Performance Period relating to the Plan Year in which he or she is promoted. For Performance Periods ending before January 1, 2020, notwithstanding Subsections (b)(1) and (b)(2) above, an Eligible Executive shall not be eligible to defer Bonus Compensation for a Plan Year unless (i) the Bonus Compensation is contingent on the satisfaction of organizational or individual performance criteria for the Performance Period that relates to the Plan Year, (ii) such criteria have been established in writing by not later than 90 days after the beginning of the applicable Performance Period, and (iii) the Bonus Compensation otherwise satisfies the requirements for performance-based compensation under Section 409A. To be effective in deferring Base Compensation or Bonus Compensation, an Eligible Executive’s Election Form must set forth the percentage of Base Compensation or Bonus Compensation (whichever applies) to be deferred, the deferral period under Section 4.03, the form of payment under Section 4.04, and any other information that may be required by the Plan Administrator from time to time. It is contemplated that an Eligible Executive will specify the investment choice under Section 5.02 (in multiples of 1%) for the Eligible Executive’s deferral, but this is not a condition for making an effective election. An Eligible Executive must make a deferral election for a Plan Year with respect to Base Compensation no later than December 31 of the year prior to the Plan Year in which the Base Compensation would otherwise be paid. If December 31 (or an applicable earlier day) is not a business day, the deadline shall be the nearest preceding day that is a business day. Notwithstanding the prior two sentences, the Plan Administrator may adopt policies and procedures that encourage or require earlier submission of Election Forms, but in which case any requirement for earlier submission may be waived (but not beyond the date specified by the first sentence of this subsection) by the Plan Administrator to prevent undue hardship for one or more Eligible Executives. Any changes in such policies or procedures or in established waiver practices from those applicable on January 1, 2019 shall be subject to Section 7.06. For Plan Years ending before January 1, 2020, subject to the last sentence of Section 3.01(a)(2) and (for later Plan Years) Section 3.05, an individual who newly becomes an Eligible Executive will have 30 days from the date the individual becomes an Eligible Executive to make a deferral election with respect to Base Compensation that is earned for services performed after the election is received (the “30-Day Election Period”). The 30-Day Election Period may be used to make an election for Base Compensation that otherwise would be paid in the Plan Year in which the individual becomes an Eligible Executive. In addition, the 30-Day Election Period may be used to make an election for Base Compensation that would otherwise be paid in the next Plan Year (i.e., the Plan Year following when the individual becomes an Eligible Executive), if the individual becomes an Eligible Executive not later than December 31 of a Plan Year. Thus, if a Base Compensation deferral election for a Plan Year is made in reliance on the 30-day rule, then the Plan Administrator shall apply the restriction that the election may only apply to Base Compensation earned for services performed after the date the election is received by the Recordkeeper. In the case of an Eligible Executive’s Bonus Compensation that relates to a Performance Period ending after December 31, 2019, an Eligible Executive must make a deferral election with respect to such Bonus Compensation no later than the last day of the Company’s fiscal year that ends just before such Performance Period. If the last day of such fiscal year is not a business day, the deadline shall be the nearest preceding day that is a business day. In the case of an Eligible Executive’s Bonus Compensation that relates to a Performance Period ending before December 31, 2019, the Eligible Executive must make a deferral election with respect to his or her Bonus Compensation at least six months prior to the end of the Performance Period for which the applicable Bonus Compensation is paid, and this election will be the Eligible Executive’s bonus deferral election for the Plan Year to which the Performance Period relates. This applies to both continuing Eligible Executives and individuals who newly become Eligible Executives. Accordingly, if an individual becomes an Eligible Executive during a Plan Year as a result of a promotion and is eligible to defer Bonus Compensation under Section 4.01(b) for such Plan Year, such Eligible Executive must make a deferral election for Bonus Compensation that is earned for the Performance Period that relates to the Plan Year in which he or she is promoted at least six months prior to the end of the applicable Performance Period. Notwithstanding the provisions in Paragraphs (1) and (2) above, the Plan Administrator may adopt policies and procedures that encourage or require earlier submission of Election Forms, but in which case any requirement for earlier submission may be waived (but not beyond the date otherwise applicable under Paragraph (1) and (2) above) by the Plan Administrator to prevent undue hardship for one or more Eligible Executives. Any changes in such policies or procedures or in established waiver practices from those applicable on January 1, 2019 shall be subject to Section 7.06. For purposes of Section 3.01 and this Section 4.02, the period of time to make the deferral election described under (a) and (b) above shall be referred to as the Deferral Window. A separate deferral election under (a) or (b) above must be made by an Eligible Executive for each category of a Plan Year’s compensation that is eligible for deferral. If a properly completed and executed Election Form is not actually received by the Recordkeeper (or, if authorized, the Plan Administrator) by the deadline applicable under Subsections (a) and (b) above, the Eligible Executive will be deemed to have elected not to defer any Base Compensation or Bonus Compensation, as the case may be, for the applicable Plan Year or the Performance Period that relates to the Plan Year, as applicable. Except as provided below in this Subsection, an election is irrevocable by the Eligible Employee once received and determined by the Plan Administrator to be properly completed (and such determination shall be made not later than the last date for making the election in question). The Plan Administrator, however, may cancel elections that have been received and accepted for a Plan Year up until the end of the day on the December 31 that precedes such Plan Year. Increases or decreases in the amount or percentage a Participant has elected to defer shall not be permitted during a Plan Year. Notwithstanding the foregoing, effective as of January 1, 2008, if a Participant receives a hardship distribution under a cash or deferred profit sharing plan that is sponsored by a member of the PepsiCo Organization and such plan requires that deferrals under such plan be suspended for a period of time following the hardship distribution, the Plan Administrator may cancel the Participant’s deferral election under this Plan so that no deferrals shall be made during such suspension period. If an election is cancelled because of a hardship distribution in accordance with the prior sentence, such cancellation shall permanently apply to the deferral election or elections for any Plan Year covered by such suspension period and the Participant will only be eligible to make a new deferral election for the Plan Year that begins after the end of the suspension period, and such new election shall be made in accordance with the rules of Sections 4.01 and 4.02. A Participant may designate on the Election Form (or in some other manner authorized by the Plan Administrator) one or more Beneficiaries to receive payment, in the event of his or her death, of the amounts credited to his or her Account; provided that, to be effective, any Beneficiary designation must be in writing, signed by the Participant, and must meet such other standards (including any requirement for spousal consent) as the Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper shall require from time to time. The Beneficiary designation must also be filed with the Recordkeeper (or the Plan Administrator for periods prior to June 3, 2002) prior to the Participant’s death. An incomplete Beneficiary designation, as determined by the Recordkeeper or Plan Administrator, shall be void and of no effect. In determining whether a Beneficiary designation that relates to the Plan is in effect, unrevoked designations that were received under the Pre-409A Program or prior to the Effective Date shall be considered. A Beneficiary designation of an individual by name remains in effect regardless of any change in the designated individual’s relationship to the Participant. Solely for periods prior to June 3, 2002, a Beneficiary designation solely by relationship (for example, a designation of “spouse,” that does not give the name of the spouse) shall designate whoever is the person in that relationship to the Participant.

A Beneficiary designation must be in writing and signed by the Participant to be effective, and must meet any additional standards—such as spousal consent—required by the Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper from time to time. The designation must be filed with the Recordkeeper (or the Plan Administrator for periods prior to June 3, 2002) before the Participant’s death; an incomplete designation, as determined by the Recordkeeper or Plan Administrator, is void and has no effect. When determining whether a Beneficiary designation is in effect, unrevoked designations received under the Pre-409A Program or prior to the Effective Date are considered. A Beneficiary designation by name remains in effect regardless of changes in the designated individual’s relationship to the Participant. For periods prior to June 3, 2002, a designation by relationship (such as “spouse” without naming the spouse) designates the person in that relationship at the time of the Participant’s death; however, any designation by relationship submitted to the Recordkeeper from and after June 3, 2002 is not effective and is void. If multiple Beneficiaries are specified and no percentages are assigned, each Beneficiary without a percentage receives an equal share of the portion of the Account not designated. A Participant may change a Beneficiary designation at any time by submitting a written, signed document filed with the Recordkeeper prior to death and meeting any required standards. An individual ceases to be a Beneficiary when all payments from the Account have been made. If a Beneficiary survives the Participant but dies before the full distribution of their interest, the Plan Administrator shall direct the Recordkeeper to pay the remaining interest to the Beneficiary’s estate. An Eligible Executive making a deferral election must specify a deferral period on their Election Form by choosing either a Specific Payment Date or the date of Separation from Service. The deferral period cannot end later than the Executive’s 80th birthday, regardless of whether the payment is a lump sum or installments. For Base Compensation paid from and after January 1, 2008, the minimum deferral period is at least 12 months after the end of the Plan Year during which the compensation would have been paid; for Bonus Compensation paid from and after January 1, 2008, the minimum is at least 18 months after the date the bonus would have been paid. If a Specific Payment Date is not specified or is less than the minimum, the Executive is deemed to have elected the minimum period. For a deferral to a Specific Payment Date, if the Election Form fails to specify a deferral period or specifies one less than the minimum, the Specific Payment Date is deemed to be the minimum period as defined in (a) and (b). An Eligible Executive may specify a form of payment—either a lump sum or installment payments—on their Election Form, with installment payments limited to a period of no more than 20 years and not later than the Executive’s 80th birthday. Installment payments must specify the frequency (quarterly, semi-annually, or annually) and whether they are fixed dollar amounts or for a fixed number of years. Fixed dollar amount installments are paid based on the selected frequency and amount until the Deferral Subaccount is exhausted, but not beyond 20 years or the Executive’s 80th birthday. If installments extend beyond the Executive’s 80th birthday or beyond 20 years, the election is treated as ending on the 80th birthday or at the end of 20 years, whichever comes first, and the amounts prior to that date are determined as if the installments continue for the full elected period, with the remaining balance distributed on the 80th birthday or at the end of 20 years. A Participant who made a valid initial deferral may make additional elections regarding the time or form of payment through a “Second Look Election.” Before January 1, 2020, a Participant could make only one Second Look Election per individual deferral of Base or Bonus Compensation. A Second Look Election must comply with the conditions in (a) and meet the following requirements: (1) If the initial election was based on a Specific Payment Date, the Second Look Election must be made at least 12 months before the original (or last previously elected) Specific Payment Date and must delay payment to a new Specific Payment Date at least five years after the original date; (2) If the initial election was based on Separation from Service, the Second Look Election must be made at least 12 months before Separation from Service and only if the separation is for Retirement, and must delay payment for at least five years—either by selecting a Specific Payment Date at least five years after the later of (i) Separation from Service or (ii) the last designated period following Separation from Service, or by delaying for five years or more following the later of (A) Separation from Service or (B) the end of the last period following Separation from Service; if a five-year delay is made and the new Specific Payment Date is less than five years after Separation from Service (or later, the last designated period), the election is void and payment is made based on the original election; (3) Before January 1, 2013, neither Separation from Service nor a delay after Separation from Service could be specified as the payout date from a Second Look Election; (4) A Participant may make an unlimited number of Second Look Elections for each individual deferral, provided each complies with the requirements of this Section; (5) If a Participant changes from lump sum to installments, the installment payments must begin no earlier than five years after the lump sum would have been paid under the initial election (or any subsequent Second Look Election), and no installment payments may be made after the Participant’s 80th birthday; (6) If a Participant changes the frequency or number of years for installment payments, the first payment date must be no earlier than five years after the first payment date under the initial (or subsequent) installment election, and no payments may occur after the 80th birthday; (7) If a Participant changes from installments to a lump sum, the lump sum must be paid no earlier than five years after the first installment payment date under the initial (or subsequent) installment election; (8) All installment payments related to a specific deferral are treated as a single payment. A Second Look Election is void and payment is made based on the original election under Sections 4.03 and 4.04 if all provisions are not satisfied. If the Second Look Election is effective, the original (or subsequent) election is superseded, including any Specific Payment Date, and is not considered for that deferral. Each Participant is solely responsible for making a Second Look Election by contacting the Recordkeeper (or, if authorized, the Plan Administrator) and complying with the requirements. The Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper may provide notice of a Second Look Election opportunity to some or all Participants, but they have no obligation to provide such notice or to provide it to all Participants. The Recordkeeper and Plan Administrator have no discretion to waive or modify any requirement for a Second Look Election set forth in this Section or in Section 409A. Each Participant has at least one separate Deferral Subaccount for each deferral of Base or Bonus Compensation. A deferral is credited to the Participant’s Account as soon as administratively practicable after the date the compensation would have been paid absent deferral. The Account is a bookkeeping device to track the value of deferrals and the Employer’s liability; no assets are reserved, segregated, insured, or secured. As of each Valuation Date, the Account is credited with earnings and gains (and debited for expenses and losses) as if the amounts had been actually invested, based on the Participant’s investment direction; these are hypothetical and not actual, but are used to measure the Account value and the Employer’s liability. Each Deferral Subaccount is invested on a phantom basis in any combination of phantom investment options selected by the Participant (or their Beneficiary after death) from those offered by the Plan Administrator. The Plan Administrator may discontinue any phantom investment option and provide rules for transferring a Participant’s phantom investment to a replacement option, unless the Participant selects another. The basic phantom investment options are: (1) Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund, where an amount is converted to phantom units by dividing by the NAV on the Valuation Date, and the value is determined by multiplying the number of phantom units by the NAV on the Valuation Date; adjustments for corporate events like stock splits or mergers are made as determined by the Plan Administrator, and no actual shares are purchased or held, and no shareholder rights are granted; (2) Phantom AFR Fund, established effective December 29, 2006, which accrues a return based on 120% of the applicable Federal long-term rate (as published by the IRS) compounded annually, with monthly accruals based on the rate in effect on the first business day of each month; (3) Other phantom investment options, designated from time to time by the Plan Administrator, which are described in provided materials and administered under procedures set by the Plan Administrator; unless otherwise specified, for unitized funds, an amount is converted to phantom units by dividing by the NAV on the Valuation Date, and the value is determined by multiplying the number of phantom units by the NAV on the Valuation Date. A Participant may allocate deferrals in one percent increments among the available phantom investment options on their Election Form. If an original election specifies less than 100% of the deferral, the Recordkeeper allocates the remaining amount to the Phantom AFR Fund to ensure 100% investment. If an original election specifies more than 100%, the Recordkeeper prorates the allocations to reduce the total to 100% after rounding to whole percents. A Participant may reallocate previously deferred amounts in a Deferral Subaccount by properly completing and submitting a fund transfer.

A Participant’s interest in the value of their Account is always 100 percent vested and will not be forfeited due to Separation from Service. In such cases, the Participant will only be eligible to receive a distribution equal to the lesser of (a) the aggregate amount of their Base Compensation and Bonus Compensation deferrals made on or after the 2006 Plan Year for Bonus Compensation and the 2007 Plan Year for Base Compensation (the “Affected Deferrals”), or (b) the net value of the Affected Deferrals as of the date the Plan Administrator determines misconduct occurred. This subsection governs the distribution of a deferral that (i) is wholly or partly invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund at the time the deferral is valued to determine the cash amount to be distributed, (ii) either was subject to a Second Look Election or was not covered by an agreement made at the time of the original deferral election that any investments in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund would remain in that fund until distribution, (iii) is made to a Participant subject to Section 16 of the Act at the time the interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund is liquidated, and (iv) if paid at the time of distribution without regard to this subsection, would result in a violation of Section 16 of the Act due to an opposite way transaction (either as a “discretionary transaction” under Rule 16b-3(b)(1) or as a regular transaction) that would be matched with the liquidation of the Participant’s interest in the PepsiCo Common Stock Fund (a “Covered Distribution”). In the case of a Covered Distribution, if the liquidation of the Participant’s interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund in connection with the distribution has not received Board Approval by the time the distribution is scheduled, the distribution shall not proceed.

A distribution to a Participant is considered a "Covered Distribution" if (i) the distribution is made to a Participant who is subject to Section 16 of the Act at the time the interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund would be liquidated, (ii) either was the subject of a Second Look Election or was not covered by an agreement made at the time of the Participant’s original deferral election that any investments in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund would remain in that fund until distribution, (iii) if paid at the time the distribution would be made without regard to this subsection, could result in a violation of Section 16 of the Act because there is an opposite way transaction that would be matched with the liquidation of the Participant’s interest in the PepsiCo Common Stock Fund (either as a “discretionary transaction” within the meaning of Rule 16b-3(b)(1), or as a regular transaction, as applicable), and (iv) the liquidation of the Participant’s interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund in connection with the distribution has not received Board Approval by the time the distribution would be made if it were not a Covered Distribution, or if it is a discretionary transaction. In such cases, the actual distribution to the Participant shall be delayed only until the earlier of: (1) in the case of a transaction that is not a discretionary transaction, Board Approval of the liquidation of the Participant’s interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund in connection with the distribution, and (2) the date the distribution would no longer violate Section 16 of the Act, such as when the Participant is no longer subject to Section 16 of the Act, when the Deferral Subaccount related to the distribution is no longer invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund, or when the time between the liquidation and an opposite way transaction is sufficient. Any notice of a denial of benefits shall advise the Claimant of the basis for the denial, pertinent Plan provisions on which the denial is based, any additional material or information necessary for the Claimant to perfect his or her claim, and the steps which the Claimant must take to appeal his or her claim for benefits. Each Claimant whose claim for benefits has been denied may file a written appeal for a review of his or her claim by the Plan Administrator. The request for review must be filed by the Claimant within 60 days after he or she received the notice denying his or her claim. Upon review, the Plan Administrator shall provide the claimant a full and fair review of the claim, including the opportunity to submit to the Plan Administrator comments, document, records and other information relevant to the claim, and the Plan Administrator’s review shall take into account such comments, documents, records and information regardless of whether it was submitted or considered at the initial determination. The decision of the Plan Administrator will be communicated to the Claimant within 60 days after receipt of a request for appeal. The notice shall set forth the basis for the Plan Administrator’s decision. However, if special circumstances require an extension of time for processing the appeal, the Plan Administrator will furnish notice of the extension to the Claimant prior to the termination of the initial 60-day period (indicating the special circumstances that require the extension), and such extension may not exceed one additional, consecutive 60-day period. The Plan Administrator may designate any division of the Company, subsidiary, or affiliate related to the Company by ownership that is part of the PepsiCo Organization as an Employer, and the Administrator’s determination of such status is absolutely conclusive. The Plan uses singular/plural and gender inclusively, and any example or use of “including” is construed as “without limitation.” The Plan benefits the parties and their successors, heirs, and assigns, but amounts credited to a Participant’s Account are not subject to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer, assignment, pledge, encumbrance, charge, garnishment, execution, or levy, and any such attempt is null and void. The Plan Administrator may make payments in accordance with a divorce decree, judgment, or court order as cash payments are made from the Deferral Subaccount, and such payments reduce the Participant’s Account. If a Participant or Beneficiary is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may direct the Employer to make payments to the person or their legal representative or apply payments for their benefit, and such payments fully discharge any liability under the Plan. The 409A Program was first adopted and approved by the Compensation Committee of PepsiCo, Inc.’s Board of Directors on November 18, 2005. It was amended and restated effective January 1, 2019, pursuant to authorization from the Compensation Committee on September 25, 2019, and again amended and restated effective January 1, 2022. The document was signed by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer of PepsiCo, Inc., on December 19, 2022, and approved by Stacy Grindal, Sr. Legal Director, Compensation and Benefits Counsel, and Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel, both on December 9, 2022. Nothing in this Article overrides Section 3.04 of the Plan or confers rights not specifically authorized. Appendix Article C addresses the termination and liquidation of the 409A Program for Participants affected by the “Closing” of the “Transaction” as defined in the Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021. The “Closing” is the consummation of the Transaction as specified in Section 2.3 of the Agreement, and the “Transaction” results in a change in control under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(i)(5). The 409A Program is irrevocably terminated with respect to all Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023, 12 months after the Closing, and the Plan sponsor retains the right to revoke this termination prior to that date. If not revoked, the termination becomes irrevocable on January 18, 2023. Each Affected Participant will receive a single lump sum payment of their entire unpaid interest under the 409A Program as of January 1, 2024, and no later than January 17, 2024, in accordance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), including any remaining installments or distributions due at a future date. The value of the interest on the January 1, 2024 distribution date is determined using the Plan’s regular valuation rules for lump sum distributions as in effect on that date.

If the termination under Section C.3 becomes irrevocable, each Affected Participant will receive their entire unpaid interest under the 409A Program as a single lump sum on January 1, 2024, and in no case later than January 17, 2024, in full compliance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). This distribution will include all remaining installments or other payments that would otherwise be due and payable to the Affected Participant at a future date. The value of the remaining interest on January 1, 2024, will be determined according to the 409A Program’s standard valuation rules for lump sum distributions as they were in effect on that date.
